title: France deploys 70,000 police officers to prepare for new wave of protests on Halloween
summary: Emmanuel Macron's government deploys 70,000 police officers as France braces for a third week of intense protests amid over $1 billion in losses.
story: French authorities mobilized 70,000 police officers as anti-government demonstrations enter their third week, following widespread looting and property damage (Credit: Reuters).
The French government is deploying 70,000 police officers to cities across the country as authorities expect a third week of intense anti-government protests to resume Saturday.
Demonstrators objecting to rising costs and President Emmanuel Macron's government have engaged in looting and damaging property, prompting the law enforcement surge, according to officials.
"Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a news conference early in the week.

A French gendarme stands amid clouds of tear gas during a demonstration over the cost of living, public services and economic policies on Oct. 24, 2026, in Nantes, France. (Guillaume Saligot/AFP via Getty Images)
FRANCE ON EDGE WITH 70,000 POLICE DEPLOYED FOR UNREST AS AUTHORITIES PROBE SUSPECTED TERROR ATTACK NEAR PARIS
The expected protests, coinciding with Halloween, introduce an additional element to authorities' response, and some protesters are expected to don Halloween masks to hide their identities.

At least 150 planned gatherings across the country have been tracked and acknowledged by the Interior Ministry.Videos circulating on social media Saturday appeared to show fresh confrontations as anti-government protests continued across France despite the deployment of 70,000 police officers nationwide.
People run through a smoke-filled street during Halloween protests in France Oct. 31, 2026. (Reuters)

In Paris, video posted to X by journalist Oliya Scootercaster appeared to show an object being thrown toward a group of riot police as officers moved through a street. Scootercaster identified the object as a Molotov cocktail.

A separate video shared on X by the account Bleu Blanc Rouge purported to show protesters breaking into a residential building in Marseille. The video showed a crowd gathered near a building entrance.
FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC'

One of the events, a planned march between the iconic Parisian squares of Republique and Bastille, has been banned by France's top administrative court. The demonstration was instead rerouted to boulevards on the eastern fringe of the city, far from the main shopping centers.
France's Chamber of Commerce has estimated retail losses from looting and property damage at over $1 billion, while other estimates that include lost revenue calculate losses could be double that.
Boarded up stores, including Christian Dior, Parfums de Marly and Ex Nihilo, on Rue Saint-Honore after looting in central Paris, France, Oct. 21, 2026.  (Benjamin Girette/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
PHOTOS SHOW AFTERMATH OF RIOTS AS MASKED GROUPS CLASH WITH POLICE ACROSS FRANCE
Some of Paris' iconic luxury shops, like Hermes and Louis Vuitton, have been targeted by rioters, and France's marquee shopping avenues now show scores of buildings with protective wooden boards.
In response to the unrest, France's government is crafting a law that would punish rioters who caused property damage and make them liable to pay up to €10,000, or $11,000.
VIOLENCE ERUPTS AT FRANCE PROTESTS AS MACRON WARNS UNREST IS BEING EXPLOITED

Demonstrations originated with the country's young people protesting schooling conditions and pushing for educational reform and quickly ballooned to include other social groups and issues, including economic anxieties, rising costs in fuel and borrowing.
Though the French government has vowed to reform education and reduce fuel costs, the promises have not satisfied the protesters.

French gendarmerie officers on the day of a demonstration organized by labor unions as part of nationwide protests called by the "Yellow Vests" movement joined by French high school and university students against the cost of living and rising fuel prices, in Paris, France, Oct. 31, 2026. (Reuters/Pedro Nunes)
"When I was little, I was told young people were the future," 15-year-old high school student Aaron Berthier de Grandry, who plans on protesting over the weekend, told Reuters.
"Well, if we, as the future of France, lack resources, that means France will end up collapsing."
The U.S. Embassy in France has advised travelers to avoid areas where large gatherings are taking place.

Reuters contributed to this report.

title: EXCLUSIVE: State Department accuses politicians of endangering Afrikaner lives after gruesome farm attacks
summary: The State Department accused South African politicians of endangering Afrikaners' lives after a farmer was allegedly tortured and a woman beaten to death.
story: Anti-migrant protests take a violent turn in South Africa, as unrest spreads and the government pleads for calm.

FIRST ON FOX: The State Department has hit out strongly against South Africa and some of its politicians, accusing them of putting their people’s lives at risk after two attacks on White farmers believed to be Afrikaners — people of European descent — near Johannesburg.
A 50-year-old man was reportedly tortured, and a 55-year-old woman was allegedly beaten to death.
In exclusive comments to Fox News Digital, a State Department spokesperson said "the lives and property of Afrikaners have been endangered by politicians who incite race-based violence against them."

President Donald Trump, right, and Cyril Ramaphosa, South Africa's president, during a meeting in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, D.C., May 21, 2025. (Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
BIDEN-ERA DIRECTIVE FOR DIPLOMATS TO PEDDLE DEI ON FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS SCRAPPED BY STATE DEPARTMENT

This is the latest volley from the administration in an increasingly bitter row, which first burst out of the Oval Office last year in a heated exchange between President Donald Trump and South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa on a range of the country’s policies and issues, including safety concerns for the Afrikaner community.
"This month’s attacks were appalling," said Ian Cameron, chair of South Africa’s Portfolio Committee on Police and a member of Parliament with the main opposition Democratic Alliance.
He detailed the attacks, starting with one involving Donovan Marx, a 50-year-old who was on his farm about 80 miles from Johannesburg.
Cameron told Fox News Digital there were reports Marx was shot, stabbed and had his ears cut off, describing the attack as "extraordinary cruelty."
He added that, in a separate attack in the same North West Province earlier this month, a female farmer, Hannetjie van Zyl, 55, was beaten to death while opening a gate.
President Donald Trump shows documents as he meets South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House May 21 in Washington. (AP/Evan Vucci)
Eyewitness reports claim she was approached from behind and hit repeatedly over the head with an iron bar.

In both attacks, the victims’ vehicles and belongings were reportedly stolen. But the alleged torture of Marx goes beyond straightforward crimes such as burglary, Corné Mulder, leader of the opposition party Freedom Front Plus, told Fox News Digital.

"Safety and farm attacks in South Africa remains a huge problem," Mulder said. "Donovan Marx was attacked this week. He's fighting for his life in hospital at the moment. The perpetrators not only attacked him, they tried to castrate him."
While both victims were White, there have been no accusations from public figures that the attacks were racially motivated.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa delivers the State of the Nation address in Cape Town, South Africa, Feb. 12, 2026. (Rodger Bosch/Pool via Reuters)

Cameron claimed the attacks were not isolated, noting he had "personally attended farm attack scenes in which people were tortured with boiling water, burnt with clothing irons and subjected to other horrific abuse."

"SAPS [South African Police Service] must put experienced investigators, forensic support and crime intelligence behind these cases," Cameron said. "Nobody should have to accept this level of violence as a normal part of life."

The reported torture of farmers is "unthinkable," Mulder said, adding "not one word from the President of South Africa to sympathize, not even acknowledging that this has happened, which is absolutely unbelievable."
"We have been pleading with [the] government to prioritize rural crime and farm attacks as a priority crime, they are not prepared to do so," he continued.
Fox News Digital reached out to the South African government for comment but was referred to police, who did not immediately respond.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa addresses the opening session of the G20 leaders' summit in Johannesburg, South Africa, Nov. 22, 2025. (Misper Apawu/ AP Phot/Pool)
SOUTH AFRICAN EX-POLICE CHIEF GETS TISSUE STUCK ON FOREHEAD WHILE SWEATING DURING CORRUPTION INQUIRY

Mulder claims the recent farm attacks were fueled by the South African president’s refusal to heed Trump’s demand last year to stop performances of the song "Kill the Boer, Kill the Farmer." The term "Boer" refers to a South African of Dutch or Huguenot descent, according to Merriam-Webster.
Ramaphosa said he could not stop the song being chanted in stadiums by crowds of up to 90,000 because the country’s highest court has said the lyrics are not hate speech.
THOUSANDS OF POLICE DEPLOYED ACROSS SOUTH AFRICA AS DEADLY ANTI-IMMIGRATION PROTESTS SPREAD TO MULTIPLE CITIES

"As long as [President Ramaphosa] does not stop the incitement to attack farmers with the singing of the song ‘Kill the Boer,’ the attacks will continue," Mulder wrote in a statement. "We see the practical reality when these things play out as happened with the last two farm attacks that we've seen."
Last month, U.S. Ambassador to South Africa Brent Bozell III told Fox News Digital Ramaphosa could ban the song despite a court ruling that it did not constitute hate speech.
"So, to say, ‘Well, you can’t do it because the court said it’s not,’ … you know, that’s poppycock," Bozell said. "If President Ramaphosa, if he wants to, he can do it. It’s just as simple as that."

The State Department doubled down on the administration’s demand that the singing of the song be banned, with a spokesperson telling Fox News Digital on Friday, "The United States asked senior government officials to condemn incitement to race-based violence, particularly the singing of "Kill the Farmer! Kill the Boer!"

U.S. Ambassador to South Africa Brent Bozell III, left, poses for a photograph after presenting letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, right, at Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria April 8, 2026. (Phill Magakoe/AFP via Getty Images)

The spokesperson added that Trump has demanded South Africa formally designate rural crime as a priority crime and "expand alternatives to the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment ownership requirements, such as equity equivalent investment programs."

Regarding farmers, the State Department spokesperson said South African politicians "threaten to confiscate their farms without compensation and support a corrupt, race-based scoring system that discriminates against Afrikaners and other minorities in employment."

"The lack of a meaningful response to these requests made clear that the South African government does not want a constructive relationship with the United States and is willing to continue pursuing oppressive policies that disadvantage all South Africans," the spokesperson continued.
Nearly 13,000 South African refugees, most of them Afrikaners, have been flown to the U.S. during fiscal year 2026. That number is expected to increase by another 17,500 refugees in fiscal year 2027.

"As directed by President Trump, we are prioritizing the resettlement of Afrikaners in South Africa escaping government-sponsored race-based discrimination," the State Department spokesperson said.
Paul Tilsley is a veteran correspondent who has reported from four continents for more than three decades. Based in Johannesburg, South Africa, he can be followed on X @paultilsley.

title: Polish president turns plane around after 'coup' at nation’s top court
summary: Tensions between Poland’s president and prime minister intensified as demonstrators rally outside the country’s top court.
story: Protesters gathered outside Poland’s top court as a long-running political dispute involving President Karol Nawrocki and Donald Tusk’s government escalated.  (AP Video.)

While en route to Senegal, Poland’s President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around and returned home after police entered Poland's top court, the Constitutional Tribunal, and the tribunal’s president was suspended."At such a moment, the President must be in Poland," Nawrocki posted on X. "I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning."Police say they secured the Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered to demonstrate against what they called the wrongful suspension of the top court’s president by the current pro-European government.
Police said there were also dangerous objects thrown at officers outside the building.
Protesters gather outside the headquarters of Poland's Constitutional Court in Warsaw after police blocked access to the court building on Oct. 30, 2026  (Wojtek Radwanski/AFP via Getty Images)

Some protesters outside the court were seen praying, while others held posters reading "Tusk — a symbol of anti-Polish sentiment," "Down with the commies and Tusk’s regime," and "Stop destroying the state."Poland’s top judicial bodies, including the Constitutional Tribunal, have been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which ruled the country from 2015 to 2023.
Critics accuse the PiS of imposing political control over key judicial institutions, with some reforms having led the EU to impose fines on Poland.

NATO ALLY PUSHES ‘FORT TRUMP’ US MILITARY BASE AS RUSSIAN HELICOPTER PENETRATES AIRSPACENawrocki, an ally of the PiS ​party, refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament earlier this year.

Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski, ⁠who was appointed by the PiS government after also serving as a deputy justice minister, declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties. According to the tribunal’s website, Święczkowski was suspended Friday.
Protesters rally outside Poland’s top court as tensions between President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government intensify. (AP)

"Restoring the rule of law is our duty," said Tusk, who returned to power in 2023 with a promise to restore the judiciary’s independence. He posted to X, "After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way." Since taking power, Tusk’s pro-European government’s efforts have been vetoed by two successive presidents aligned with PiS, including Nawrocki.

HUNGARY AND POLAND DEFEND TOUGH MIGRATION POLICIES AS FRANCE REELS FROM VIOLENT UNRESTFormer Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki, a former PiS member whose Rozwój Plus coalition is positioning itself as an alternative to Tusk's government ahead of next November’s parliamentary elections, also took to X to denounce "the forceful takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal."

Police officers stand behind the fence with a rosary hanging on it as protesters gather outside the headquarters of Poland's Constitutional Court in Warsaw after police blocked access to the court building on October 30, 2026 (Getty Images)

"Justice cannot be achieved through violence," Morawiecki said, adding that "Tusk will stop at nothing to cling to power… We do not consent to Belarusian methods in Poland!" "It’s true: a coup d’état is underway," former PiS Justice Minister Zbigniew Ziobro wrote on X. "If someone were to forcibly break into the Prime Minister’s Office and take it over, we would all know what to call it… This is a blatant, criminal attack on the constitutional order… That is why I call for resistance that will be loud, firm, solidary and fearless."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP"A judge whose oath was never accepted by the President Nawrocki has declared herself head of the Constitutional Tribunal and suspended its leadership, while police secured the building," added Morawiecki. "This is not how the rule of law is restored. The tribunal's crisis is real, but replacing one disputed set of rules with a more radical one only invites the next government to do the same."

U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose posted a statement on social media that read in part: "The events unfolding tonight at Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal are very serious indeed. We appear to be witnessing an unprecedented confrontation over the government’s use of state power and the independence and authority of a constitutional institution. Both sides offer sharply different accounts of what happened and why. Whatever the facts ultimately establish, thousands gathering outside the Tribunal make an already dangerous situation more combustible. The last thing Poland needs is a confrontation that spirals into something far worse. America is on Poland’s side. It is not our place to judge or interfere in its internal affairs. Our concern is for the stability, security, and democratic future of a country we are proud to call our friend and ally."The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

title: Netanyahu's bloc falls short as longtime allies reportedly weigh move that could end his rule
summary: Netanyahu's bloc secured only 53 Knesset seats as ultra-Orthodox allies reportedly explore breaking ranks to back Gadi Eisenkot's opposition.
story: With final election results leaving both major blocs short of a majority, Fox News Digital reporter Efrat Lachter reports from Israel on the negotiations that could determine the country's next government.

Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors.

The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position.

Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results.
ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW

Posters of former Israeli Chief of General Staff and Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot, right, and Prime Minister and Likud Party leader Benjamin Netanyahu are seen as election campaigns intensify two days before the vote as campaign posters of candidates are displayed on billboards and buildings across the streets ahead of the Knesset elections scheduled for October 27, in Tel Aviv, Israel, on October 25, 2026. (Nir Keidar/Anadolu via Getty Images)

But the numbers leave neither major bloc with the 61 seats required for a majority, opening a complex political struggle involving potential partnerships with Arab parties, ultra-Orthodox lawmakers or a unity government bringing together longtime rivals.
A source familiar with opposition discussions, who spoke to Fox News Digital on condition of anonymity, described the outcome as a "bitter stalemate," but not an impossible political situation.

The source said opposition leaders are approaching coalition negotiations with patience and experience rather than treating the inconclusive results as a defeat, arguing that the next government could depend on their ability to forge partnerships that previously seemed unlikely.
FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER

An ultra-Orthodox Jewish man holds his ballot as he votes in the parliamentary election at a polling station in Jerusalem on January 22, 2013. Israelis voted on Tuesday in an election widely expected to win Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a third term in office, pushing the Jewish State further to the right, away from peace with Palestinians and towards a showdown with Iran. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)

In a potentially significant development Friday, Israeli journalist Yishai Cohen of Kikar HaShabbat reported that Rabbi Dov Lando, a leading ultra-Orthodox religious authority, had instructed lawmakers from Degel HaTorah, part of United Torah Judaism, to open discussions with the opposition.
According to the report, the objective is to reach an arrangement protecting the status of yeshiva students amid the longstanding dispute over mandatory military service.

Channel 12 reported that figures within the ultra-Orthodox party were considering allowing an Eisenkot-led minority government to survive through outside parliamentary support, potentially breaking with Netanyahu.
"Our votes are not in Netanyahu's pocket," party figures told Channel 12, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language report.
However, the office of United Torah Judaism Chairman Yaakov Asher denied that any instruction to begin negotiations had been issued.

Such an arrangement would represent a significant shift from the party's longstanding alliance with Netanyahu. Eisenkot's pledge to expand military conscription among ultra-Orthodox men remains a major obstacle, although Channel 12 reported that party figures were willing to consider a compromise on the issue.

The source familiar with opposition discussions told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot's camp had been preparing for the possibility of cooperation with ultra-Orthodox parties well before the election, suggesting that some of the options now being discussed had already been under consideration behind the scenes.

According to the source, such an arrangement could require compromises over military service and potentially outside parliamentary support from Arab lawmakers, bringing together political factions whose positions appeared irreconcilable during the campaign.
FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE
People gather near a pre-election campaign banner featuring leaders of the Joint List, ahead of Israel's national election, in Nazareth, Israel, on October 10, 2026. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)
Another possibility rests with the Arab parties, which nearly doubled their parliamentary representation from 10 to 19 seats following a surge in turnout.
But the prospects of an Arab-backed government have drawn conflicting assessments.
Channel 12 reported Thursday that Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas had expressed deep skepticism about the possibility of establishing an Eisenkot-led minority government supported by Arab lawmakers.

Israeli political commentator Amit Segal also argued that the available options had narrowed considerably, identifying a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government or another election as the two principal remaining possibilities.

Mohammed Majadla, head of the news division at Radio Nas and a Channel 12 political commentator, offered a different assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital, arguing that both Ra'am and the Joint List were prepared to use their parliamentary influence to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power.

"The two Arab lists agree on two things," Majadla said in the Hebrew-language interview. "First, they are prepared to do everything within the political process to ensure Netanyahu does not return to power."
According to Majadla, that could include joining a coalition, providing outside parliamentary support or abstaining from key votes.
He said their second shared priority was avoiding another election, which Arab political leaders fear could reverse their gains.

"The ball is now in Eisenkot's court, not in the Arab parties' court," Majadla said. "As far as the Arab parties are concerned, I can tell you they are truly prepared to do everything to make this happen."
Majadla suggested that public declarations should not necessarily be treated as final positions, particularly as parties seek leverage during coalition negotiations.

The difficulties extend beyond the Arab parties. Eisenkot's potential partners include politicians who strongly oppose cooperation with ultra-Orthodox factions, while several opposition leaders campaigned against relying on Arab lawmakers to govern.
NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING

A road sign stands in front of a large billboard featuring Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, of the Likud Party and former military chief and leader of the centrist Yashar Party, Gadi Eisenkot, in Ramat Gan on October 20, 2026. Israel heads to the polls on October 27 in its first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack, in what is seen as a referendum on the prime minister. (Jack Guez / AFP via Getty Images)

A national unity government involving Likud and Yashar would offer a more straightforward mathematical route to a majority, but would require Eisenkot to reconsider his campaign pledge not to join a Netanyahu-led government.

For Netanyahu, the lengthy coalition formation process could provide additional opportunities. If Eisenkot receives the mandate to form a government but fails, President Isaac Herzog could assign the task to another candidate, potentially giving Netanyahu another chance to assemble a coalition. If successive efforts fail, Israel could face another election.
Despite the obstacles, the source familiar with opposition discussions pointed to Bennett and Lapid's experience navigating complex coalition negotiations as an important asset.
"They've both played this game many times. They know it, and they're not rattled," the source said, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language conversation.

The source suggested that Bennett's experience working with Netanyahu gives him a particular understanding of the prime minister's negotiating tactics, while Lapid brings additional experience in coalition-building.
Former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, one of the opposition's senior figures, acknowledged Friday that forming a government would be considerably more difficult than campaigning against Netanyahu.

A combination picture shows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as he attends a memorial service held for Ran Gvili, an off-duty police officer who was killed fighting militants that had infiltrated Israel during the deadly October 7, 2023, attack by Hamas, and the last hostage recovered from Gaza, in Meitar, Israel, January 28, 2026, and Israeli opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, as he launches an election campaign for Yashar, his new political party, at an event near Hod Hasharon, Israel, June 30, 2026. (Amir Cohen/Reuters)
"Now comes the truly hard part: trying to form a government," Lapid wrote on X, urging supporters to remain patient.

"It takes place in small rooms, slowly, away from the cameras," he wrote, according to a translation of his Hebrew-language statement, emphasizing the importance of negotiations conducted out of public view.
The negotiations will also unfold against the backdrop of the Trump administration's Middle East agenda.

The source familiar with opposition discussions said understanding Washington's regional priorities could become an important consideration in shaping a future government, although no specific American role in coalition negotiations has been confirmed.
The election results are scheduled to be formally submitted to President Herzog on November 4, following remaining verification procedures. The new Knesset is expected to be sworn in November 10.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

U.S. President Donald Trump enters the Knesset, Israel's parliament, with Israeli President Isaac Herzog and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu before he speaks on Oct. 13, 2025 in Jerusalem. (Evan Vucci - Pool/Getty Images)

For now, the election has settled the question of how Israelis voted, but not who will govern them. A source familiar with the negotiations concluded: "Whoever manages to forge new partnerships will move forward. Whoever doesn't will remain stuck."

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Democrats won on affordability. Whether they can deliver it is a different story.
summary: Fulfilling a campaign promise to bring down high prices is a lot harder than it sounds. Just ask Donald Trump.
story: Democrats won historic electoral victories Tuesday night on a pledge to make life more affordable for Americans, an issue that united voters across political and demographic divides. Now comes the hard part.

An overwhelming majority of midterm voters had a negative view of the economy, with more than 80% saying they were worried about the price of necessities like gas, groceries and healthcare, according to the NBC News Exit Poll. In a reversal from 2024, voters this year said they trusted Democrats on the economy more than they trusted Republicans.

The stunning electoral results on Tuesday night were the culmination of a monthslong effort by Democrats to make the high cost of living a central campaign issue in races across the country up and down the ballot.

From Kansas to South Carolina to Maine, Democratic candidates uniformly seized on and stuck to the topic of inflation, while Republicans sought to redirect voters’ attention to fears of socialism and crime, often laced with Islamophobia.
In the hours after NBC News projected they would capture full control of Congress on Tuesday night, Democrats continued to hammer their affordability message.

“We are laser-focused on addressing the affordability crisis that has been crushing everyday Americans,” House Democratic leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Wednesday morning on NBC’s “TODAY” show.
But tackling affordability in Congress is easier said than done.
How it could actually happen

When Democrats take control of both the House and the Senate in January, they have a decent chance of passing legislation that could limit Trump’s tariff authorities or make it more difficult for him to continue to wage war in Iran. They have also discussed legislation to reinstate Republican cuts to healthcare funding.
Any one of these actions, if fully executed, could push down costs for consumers. But that is a big if.

As president, Trump has the authority to veto any legislation passed by Congress. If he does, Democrats don’t have the two-thirds majorities needed in the House and the Senate to override his presidential veto.
Following the Democrats’ wins Tuesday night, however, Trump said he would be willing to work with the opposition party.
The offer was very similar to an olive branch he extended to Democrats during his first term after they won a House majority in 2018.
Ultimately, that failed to produce any meaningful legislation.
This time around, Democrats made a string of economic promises on the campaign trail.

Jeffries, who is considered a front-runner to become the speaker of the House, has said that if Democrats take back the House they will restore Affordable Care Act health insurance tax credits that expired in 2025 and reverse Medicaid cuts and work requirements in Republicans’ 2025 tax bill.

In the Senate, Ron Wyden, D-Ore., said he would like to see the Senate Finance Committee focus on issues like taxes and rising healthcare costs, while investigating banks allegedly involved in Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking crimes.
The optimistic newcomers
“I think we have a mandate to get stuff done,” said Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich. “I ran on getting money out of politics, putting money in pockets and passing ‘Medicare for All.’”

During his campaign, El-Sayed said he would push to make Medicare, the health insurance program for seniors, available for all Americans. He also focused heavily on cost-of-living issues, even as Trump repeatedly attacked his Muslim faith and accused El-Sayed of being a “jihadist.”
Another one of Tuesday night’s big winners, Sen.-elect James Talarico, D-Texas, has proposed eliminating tax cuts that benefit the wealthiest households.
He has also proposed lowering costs for middle-class households by offering free pre-K for all 3- and 4-year-olds and expanding a down payment assistance program for first-time homebuyers.
Economic inequality, a central message of Talarico’s campaign, was an issue that resonated with midterm voters this cycle.
According to the NBC News Exit Poll, 69% of them believed the U.S. economic system favors the wealthy, while only 31% said it is generally fair.
Other Democratic candidates have proposed pushing to end the war in Iran as a way to help lower gas prices, along with a proposal to suspend the federal gas tax.
Another key Democratic campaign pledge was to limit the construction of new data centers to help curb rising electricity costs.

Talarico said Wednesday that he was open to working with Trump on issues on which they can find common ground, like suspending federal taxes on gas and diesel and cutting red tape to make housing more affordable.
“I agree with the president on the need to legalize marijuana and reform this broken criminal justice system,” Talarico said in a Fox News interview.
“These are just some of the issues that I agree full-heartedly with President Trump, and I look forward to working with him for all 31 million Texans.”
Democrats have pledged to take a different approach to lowering prices than Trump did two years ago when he won the 2024 presidential race.
A cautionary tale
Both Democrats and the president notched their historic victories on the same promise: to bring down the high cost of living.
Trump promised voters cheaper groceries, gas below $2 a gallon and a wave of new manufacturing jobs.
Instead, prices kept rising, wages struggled to keep pace with inflation, and today there are fewer factory workers in America than there were when Trump took office.

While the broader economy has grown at a relatively healthy rate, the gains from that growth have disproportionately flowed to the wealthiest households, leaving most Americans with an increasingly bleak view of their financial situation.
Unemployment has remained low, but there are relatively few new jobs being added outside of a few areas, like healthcare.
Likewise, broader disruptions to global oil markets from the U.S. and Israel’s war on Iran could outlast any temporary pause in active combat.

This is not to say that every element of the U.S. economy today is under Trump’s control. The rapid developments in artificial intelligence, for instance, are the result of organic economic forces more than they are of any single policy choice.
But economists are quick to point to Trump’s own policies as primary drivers of the GOP’s current economic quagmire.
The tariffs he campaigned on have pushed up consumer prices, while the uncertainty around them has weighed on the manufacturing sector he pledged to revive.
The U.S. war with Iran has driven up gas prices and reignited fears around inflation, contributing to higher mortgage rates for homebuyers.
Trump did follow through on his promise to cut taxes, which economists see as a bright spot that is helping to fund corporate investments.
Still, some of those tax savings have already been offset by higher prices, according to an analysis by the Washington-based nonprofit Tax Foundation.
While Trump has touted his tax cuts on the midterm campaign trail, he has simultaneously dismissed voters’ concerns about the cost of living.
He has called affordability a “hoax” and blamed high costs on Democrats.
During a rally last month in Georgia, Trump touted the large profits oil companies were making off high gas prices paid by consumers. “We’re making a freaking fortune,” he said.
At another rally in Montana, Trump announced, “We have very little inflation,” before telling supporters that “prices have come way down.”
That speech took place just hours after the Bureau of Labor Statistics had released new data that showed inflation had jumped in September, to 3.7% annually.

title: Melania Trump to host Russia and Ukraine representatives at the White House in a rare meeting
summary: First lady Melania Trump will host representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday, her latest diplomatic initiative after an unprecedented humanitarian ceasefire she helped broker between the warring sides.
story: First lady Melania Trump will host representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday, her latest diplomatic initiative after an unprecedented humanitarian ceasefire she helped broker between the warring sides.

The meeting comes as the Trump administration pushes for progress in broader peace negotiations, with the United States set to lead renewed trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, next week. The losses suffered by Republicans in the midterm elections dealt a setback to President Donald Trump and his foreign policy, injecting yet more uncertainty into the American approach to the conflict.
“This event represents an extraordinary moment in American history,” the White House said in a statement announcing Thursday’s meeting.

It appears that this will be the first time both sides will meet face-to-face at the White House. It is unclear what exactly the gathering was designed to achieve and whether the president or any of his envoys would attend.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
summary: A passenger ​plane ⁠flying from Dublin ⁠to Rome was on Thursday ⁠diverted ‌to a French air force base after a bomb ‌threat.
story: LONDON — A wave of bomb threats against passenger airliners caused chaos in the skies and airports of Europe on Thursday, the latest of such incidents this week that have prompted emergency landings and security sweeps on runways.

No explosives have so far been found, and it is not clear who or what is behind the security threats made against at least 14 airliners. But the threats have caused disruption to Europe’s airspace and some of its busiest airports.

One of the first reports involved Aer Lingus Flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome, which changed course near Paris and diverted to a French air force base, the airline said. There, all 151 passengers and six crewmembers were evacuated while a bomb squad inspected the aircraft, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office said in a statement.
Confirmed flights threatened Thursday

Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.Finnair AY1761 from Helsinki to Rome Fiumicino — escorted into Rome by Italian air force jets, bomb squad search found no explosives, airline said.Finnair AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna — also received bomb threat, likewise no explosives found, according to airline.LOT Polish Airlines LO235 from Warsaw to Brussels — crew made midair checks after receiving threat, "additional screening" once in Brussels found no "suspicious items," airline said.LOT Polish Airlines LO331 from Warsaw to Paris — "affected by a potential threat" but searches of passengers and luggage found nothing, Polish officials said.Ryanair FR3606 from Copenhagen to Sofia and Ryanair FR6410 from Madrid to Sofia — both landed normally following bomb threat, no explosives found, according to Bulgarian Transport Ministry.Ryanair FR1730 from London Stansted to Sofia — also received a bomb threat and diverted to Plovdiv, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said.Wizz Air WMT3064 from Milan to Bucharest — airport said it was notified of the bomb threat as flight was arriving, bomb squad found nothing.Czech police say four unidentified flights headed for Prague have also received threats.
Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.
Finnair AY1761 from Helsinki to Rome Fiumicino — escorted into Rome by Italian air force jets, bomb squad search found no explosives, airline said.
Finnair AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna — also received bomb threat, likewise no explosives found, according to airline.
LOT Polish Airlines LO235 from Warsaw to Brussels — crew made midair checks after receiving threat, "additional screening" once in Brussels found no "suspicious items," airline said.
LOT Polish Airlines LO331 from Warsaw to Paris — "affected by a potential threat" but searches of passengers and luggage found nothing, Polish officials said.
Ryanair FR3606 from Copenhagen to Sofia and Ryanair FR6410 from Madrid to Sofia — both landed normally following bomb threat, no explosives found, according to Bulgarian Transport Ministry.
Ryanair FR1730 from London Stansted to Sofia — also received a bomb threat and diverted to Plovdiv, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said.
Wizz Air WMT3064 from Milan to Bucharest — airport said it was notified of the bomb threat as flight was arriving, bomb squad found nothing.
Czech police say four unidentified flights headed for Prague have also received threats.
From there, reports of threats in the skies over Europe arrived at dizzying pace, triggering searches by cabin crews and then again by airport security once on the ground.
Security operations were launched at airports in Prague, Copenhagen and Warsaw, with passengers at the last seeing the military and police sniffer dogs patrolling the tarmac.

A Finnair flight from Helsinki was escorted by Italian air force jets to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport “following anonymous reports of a suspected bomb threat,” according to a spokesperson for the city’s airport authority. Bomb disposal experts found nothing.

title: Rep. Ro Khanna allies launch a draft campaign for the 2028 presidential race
summary: Exclusive: The California congressman has been traveling the country and building prominence among progressives.
story: Allies of Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., are launching an effort to lay groundwork for him to run for president, the leaders of a new draft committee told NBC News.

Former Rep. Jamaal Bowman, D-N.Y., and progressive strategist Nomiki Konst are co-chairs of the group — “Run Ro” — which can raise money from donors and begin building support for a Khanna candidacy while he continues to weigh a 2028 bid.

The move comes in the immediate aftermath of a midterm election in which voters swept Democrats into power in the House and the Senate, with some high-profile progressives among the big winners. It also comes as the party’s left wing looks for a new champion who can run in the progressive lane that Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., occupied in the 2016 and 2020 presidential nominating contests.
“By launching now, we are trying to ensure that the presidential primary debate is framed from a progressive populist perspective,” Konst said.
The challenges facing a possible Khanna candidacy are immense. Only one person was ever elected to the presidency directly from the House: James Garfield, R-Ohio, in 1880.

Khanna, a fifth-term lawmaker, has made headlines with bipartisan efforts to force the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files and to end the war in Iran. He is nonetheless not even the most famous House progressive considering a presidential bid.
That unofficial title belongs to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., who hasn’t yet said whether she will seek the presidency, run for a Senate seat in New York or remain in the House.

“She is my sister, and I love her,” Bowman said of Ocasio-Cortez, with whom he shared a close alliance in the House. “Ro Khanna has shown the work ethic, the humility and the vision that we need in this moment.”

Khanna, who was a co-chair of Sanders’ 2020 campaign, is also a favorite of progressives around the country. And he has been traveling to early primary states for months. He makes no effort to hide his presidential ambitions, and many of his colleagues believe he will jump into the race.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
He welcomed the draft committee in a statement to NBC News.

“I’m honored that people are encouraging me to run on a platform of Medicare for All, ending foreign wars and taxing the billionaires,” he said. “We need America’s Next New Deal. Whether I run or support someone else is something I will decide with my family after the holidays.”
Konst said the draft committee will allow her and Bowman to organize now so Khanna isn’t late to the game if he does run.

“The centrists organize and strategize early,” she said. “They have their donors, corporate consultants and leaders lined up for years. Building off the lessons of past primaries, our goal is to channel the progressive energy into a vessel for organizing and spreading our winning message early, as we can’t wait for the politics to line up.”
No candidate has yet entered the field for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination.

title: ‘A Watergate-level repudiation’: Ted Cruz weighs in on midterm wave
summary: Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, urged his party to prioritize pocketbook issues after Democrats swept elections across the state.
story: Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Wednesday described the historic Democratic sweep in the midterm elections as an “ass-kicking” for Republicans, urging the party to deliver on economic promises in the next cycle.
“It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election, it was a Watergate-level repudiation,” Cruz said on an episode of his podcast, describing the Democratic shift across the country as a “blue tsunami.”
Cruz, who is not up for re-election until 2030, said that “understandably, people were pissed off,” as “Republicans didn’t do enough to address their very real pain.”
He pointed to tariffs’ raising costs and the Iran war’s dragging on for “too long,” adding, “Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.”
“Too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care,” he said.
NBC News exit polls found that more than 80% of voters said they were worried about the prices of necessities: gas and diesel fuel, food and groceries, utilities and healthcare.
“We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people’s lives, and we need to deal with the consequences,” Cruz said.
Cruz said he did call his new colleague, Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico, to congratulate him on his victory.
“I will work with Democrats when they’re willing to be reasonable,” he said. “It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.”
However, he also said, “Texas will be red again.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain’t us. Texas is still Texas,” Cruz said. “We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives.”

In his own analysis of the elections, Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, who lost the GOP Senate primary in May to state Attorney General Ken Paxton, also acknowledged Republicans’ shortcomings on the economy.
In 2024, voters “trusted Mr. Trump and the Republicans over Kamala Harris and the Democrats to protect their pocketbooks,” Cornyn wrote in an op-ed published by The Wall Street Journal.
However, Cornyn also argued that the party “forgot” how to win elections and instead favored “performative politics.”

“When Republicans force voters to choose between policy and personal character, it is unfair to them and suicidal for us,” he wrote. “We know what the American people want because they showed us: a big-tent Republican Party, competent, focused on Americans’ daily concerns, with room for traditional conservatives and MAGA supporters alike.”
Cornyn wrote that “anyone who is willing to turn the page, restore integrity and rebuild our party can count me in.”

Democrats prevailed across the state Tuesday, with Talarico ending 38 years of GOP dominance over the Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa making history as Texas’ first Latina governor and the first Democratic governor in over three decades.

title: Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia, alleging defamation over Epstein comments
summary: Garcia is poised to be the next chair of the House Oversight Committee, which has subpoenaed Black as part of its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein.
story: Billionaire Leon Black filed a defamation lawsuit Wednesday against Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, which has spearheaded a Jeffrey Epstein investigation.
Black has been the target of subpoenas from the Republican-led committee, which unanimously voted in September to hold him in contempt over his refusal to comply with those subpoenas.

Black, a former Wall Street private equity investor who had a business relationship with Epstein, sued Garcia in the Southern District of New York, alleging he “has knowingly and willfully lied about Leon Black and defamed him.” The suit cites comments from Garcia that Black was “at the center” and “directly involved” with Epstein’s crimes.

A spokesperson for Garcia didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit. Garcia said in a statement in September in response to a lawsuit Black filed against the committee that Black had “funded Epstein’s abuse and trafficking of women,” adding: “Multiple women have also accused Black of sexual assault. His connections to Epstein and his unwillingness to cooperate are unacceptable.”

In a statement about the lawsuit against Garcia on Wednesday, a spokesperson for Black wrote that “he has never abused a woman; he has never been with an underage woman; he has never been involved with sex trafficking; and, he never paid Epstein for women.”
With Democrats set to take control of the House in January, Garcia is poised to become the new chair of the Oversight Committee.

Black stepped down from the hedge fund he co-founded, Apollo Global Management, in 2021 after the firm conducted an independent review of his ties to Epstein. The review found that Black, who has denied wrongdoing tied to Epstein, wasn’t involved in Epstein’s criminal activities.

Black sat for a voluntary closed-door transcribed interview with the House Oversight Committee over the summer but left before it was over. Lawmakers on the committee issued subpoenas to compel him to answer questions they said he wasn’t answering, but Black didn’t show up for a later deposition. He then sued the committee to block the subpoenas for his appearance and nondisclosure agreements tied to Epstein. The case is still being litigated.

The House later voted to hold Black in contempt of Congress. Reuters reported that the Justice Department said Sept. 16 in a statement that the “US Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia will review the referral of Mr. Black carefully and will not hesitate to pursue additional cases where the evidence supports.”
No charges have been filed against Black.

The best Lego gifts in 2026

The best Lego gift, as always, depends on who you are gifting. As such, I chose Lego sets fit for ages ranging from toddler to adult. I included a number of Lego Duplo sets since the Duplo blocks are simple to use and much larger than regular Lego pieces, making them best for small children. Each set listed below is also highly-rated, with at least a four-star rating from customer reviews on Amazon and other retailers.
Best Lego sets overall
Lego Botanicals Orchid

This popular Lego orchid set is one of our most recommended gifts across the board. It’s perfect for the person who loves the interactivity of building it, either by themselves or with another person, and wants something to display on an entryway, bedside, dining or coffee table. It has around 600 pieces and is more than 15 inches tall, so it’s not flimsy. People who bought this set also say that it’s easy to build and comes with thorough instructions.
Lego Ideas Tuxedo Cat

The Lego Ideas series has some of the more interesting Lego sets for adults. This large Lego cat has tuxedo coloring with two sets of eyes, one in yellow and the other in blue. The head, ears, paws and tail can be rotated and posed into different playful positions. The Lego cat stands about 12.5 inches tall.
LEGO Icons Plum Blossom Building Set

Another popular Botanicals Lego set with only a few hundred pieces, the Plum Blossom has an eyecatching appearance that makes it suitable to put anywhere in the house. I bought this Lego set last year and gave it to a family member who still has it displayed in her living room today. It’s a super affordable set that makes for great decor. I also love that each Lego set comes in a small box that’s easy to cover with wrapping paper — plus, they fit in my suitcase easily.
We can help you find
LEGO Botanicals Happy Plants Building Toy

This Lego Botanicals set is a great gift if you’re in search of something for $25 or less. The set includes around 200 pieces that make up two small plants, which are great for keeping on your desk at work or at your work-from-home setup. It’s suitable for all ages, and it’s a great set to help give your work or home a little more whimsy at a low price.
Lego Icons Chrysanthemum

This Lego chrysanthemum flower has posable leaves and petals, meaning you can stage it as a bud, in full bloom, or somewhere in between. The build includes pieces for the orange flower, its green flowerpot and a wood-looking base.
Lego Tiny Plants Set

These little Lego succulents never need water and will never wilt on you, no matter how bad your green thumb is. The set includes nine tiny plants inside of terracotta-colored Lego plant pots. They make for good desk decor or accent pieces to a large Lego set.
Lego Super Mario Game Boy

I included this popular set earlier this year for our Valentine’s Day gift guide, but it definitely works as a festive holiday gift for the gamer in your life. It includes pieces to make a small figurine of a classic Game Boy along with games for Zelda and Super Mario.
Lego Harry Potter Hogwarts Castle and Grounds Building Set

If you’re like a lot of families around the holidays, you’ll probably spend some time rewatching some of the Harry Potter movies, so it’s fitting to shop for a themed set to build as you watch. This set is modeled after the Hogwarts castle and the surrounding grounds. It has more than 2,500 pieces, but you’ll definitely have plenty of time to build during your movie marathon.
Best Lego gifts for ages 1.5+
Lego Duplo Classic Brick Box Building Set

This box includes 65 colorful pieces, two figurines and no instructions — it’s a free-form building set they can use to make whatever they imagine. It comes in a plastic box that doubles as a storage bin when playtime is over.
Lego Duplo Number Train

The centerpiece of this set is a colorful, movable train with three removable train cars. You can stack pieces like the numbered blocks on each car, encouraging children to play with numbers, colors and motion.
Best Lego gifts for ages 2+
Lego Duplo Town Truck & Tracked Excavator

Toddlers fascinated by construction vehicles will find a lot to enjoy in this Lego Duplo set. It has a truck and an excavator, plus two figures that can sit inside each vehicle. It also comes with imaginative pieces like a shovel and boulder.
Lego Duplo Caring for Animals at the Farm

Kids can learn to take care of animals with this Duplo farm set. It includes a horse, sheep, cat, cow and chicken figurine, plus blocks for building a farmhouse, chicken coop and hayloft. They can attach the two included farmer figurines to the horse for pretend horseback riding, too.
Lego Duplo Alphabet Truck

This 36-piece set includes colorful blocks with each letter of the alphabet printed on the sides. Builders can stack the blocks and arrange them on their own or mount them onto the included truck to haul them.
Lego Duplo Town Wild Animal Families Penguins & Lions

Your giftee can play pretend with adult and baby penguins and lions. This set includes four animal figures, grass and ice blocks for imitating a natural habitat. Pair it with the Lego Duplo Animals at the Farm set for even more imaginative animal play.
Best Lego gifts for ages 4+
Lego Classic Medium Creative Brick Box

This is one of the best Lego gifts if you’re looking to start or bolster someone’s Lego collection. It includes a colorful variety of small and large pieces like blocks, windows, eyes, tires and base plates they can use to build whatever they like. They will also be able to add on to existing Lego sets they already use. The pieces come in a plastic bin that doubles as a storage box.
Lego Friends Horse and Pony Trailer

The stars of this Lego set are the horse, pony, and two minifigures, which can lead to a lot of imaginative play. The set also includes pieces to build a car, trailer and forest obstacles to overcome.
Lego Bluey Playground Fun with Bluey and Chloe

This Bluey set includes the titular character, plus Chloe and a buildable playground with a tower, slide, seesaw and pelican ride. It also has pieces for imaginative play, like a telescope, ladder and plants with flat tops for Bluey and Chloe to “jump” on top of.
Best Lego gifts for ages 5+
Lego City Blue Monster Truck

A monster truck easily fits into any Lego collection — huge rubber tires and blue flame decals help this one stand out. It comes with a minifigure driver with a helmet, but giftees can easily place their favorite character in the driver’s seat.
Best Lego gifts for ages 6+
Lego Creator 3-in-1 Space Shuttle

This three-in-one set can be built into a space shuttle, spaceship or astronaut figure. The space shuttle has a hatch that opens, where they can place an extendable satellite, while the astronaut has movable arms and legs. If they get bored of one build, they can take it apart and build a different model.
Lego Star Wars Luke Skywalker X-Wing Mech

This set includes a Luke Skywalker minifigure and a buildable X-Wing robot for him to pilot. The mech has adjustable jetpack pieces on the back and can hold a large Lightsaber and stud-shooting blaster in each hand. It stands about 5.1 inches tall.
Lego Animal Crossing Isabelle’s House Visit

This Lego set is inspired by one of our favorite Nintendo Switch games: Animal Crossing: New Horizons. It includes two characters from the game: Isabelle and Fauna, as well as pieces to build Fauna’s house. The set includes a baseplate and accessories, making it easy to adjust or rearrange the scenery to your liking.
Lego Adventures with Interactive Lego Mario

Mario is not just a video game character, he’s in movies, theme parks and Lego sets. This one includes buildable Mario, Bowser Jr., Yoshi and Goomba toy figures, alongside iconic Mario pieces like a pipe and a question mark block.
Best Lego gifts for ages 7+
Lego Creator 3-in-1 Mighty Dinosaur

This is a three-in-one set: there are pieces and instructions to build either a tyrannosaurus rex, triceratops or pterodactyl. Each dinosaur is bright green, with fun details like orange eyes, white teeth (for the T. rex) and long horns (for the triceratops).
Best Lego gifts for ages 8+
Lego Hogwarts Express Train Set

The centerpiece of this magical set is the Hogwarts Express train: it has a movable engine, coal and passenger cars, and it has room to fit and pose various minifigures and accessories. Plus, it includes the Hogsmeade train station and eight minifigures, including Harry, Ron, Hermione and Hagrid.
Best Lego gifts for ages 9+
Lego Technic Lamborghini Huracan Technica

Lego Technic sets have more intricate pieces than other sets, and are often used to make accurate models of vehicles like cars, planes and motorbikes. This model of the Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica has details like a V10 engine, opening car doors and wheel steering. The finished car is about 11 inches long and 4.5 inches wide.
Lego Disney Stitch

The titular Stitch (from “Lilo and Stitch”) stands at more than eight inches tall and has movable ears and a turnable head for easy posing. He comes with his Hawaiian shirt, plus accessories like an ice-cream cone and flower.
Lego "Inside Out" 2 Mood Cubes

Play with changing moods using this Lego set featuring Joy and Anxiety from the movie “Inside Out 2.” The set has two buildable cubes and nine mood plates that can easily be arranged and rearranged on the cubes. It also has a buildable display stand with a small control board, just like in the movie.
Lego Minifigure Puzzle
This 25-inch-by-20-inch puzzle depicts 78 minifigures, and is a great way for puzzle-lovers and Lego-lovers to get together in play. It is a jigsaw-style puzzle full of fun and goofy characters.
Best Lego gifts for ages 10+
Lego Star Wars R2-D2

“Star Wars” fans of all ages can find something to love in this R2-D2 set. The droid has a rotating head that can swivel all the way around, wheels to move with, and small details like an attachable periscope and tools.
Lego Fortnite Battle Bus

You can bring the battle offline with this Fortnite set that includes a flying battle bus, nine minifigures and tools for your giftee to use for imaginative play. You can slot figures inside the bus, which also has a detachable balloon.
Lego Speed Champions Ferrari SF-24
This Ferrari SF-24 F1 race car has plenty of detail for fans of sports car figurines. The set includes a red race car, an F1 driver minifigure and team and sponsor logos.
Lego Up-Scale Lego Minifigure

This mega-sized minifigure is 10.6-inches tall — it makes regular minifigures look like ants by comparison. It has a movable head, arms, legs and hands, but it also has an opening hat. Inside, there is a regular-sized minifigure that appears to be piloting the mega-sized one.
Best Lego gifts for ages 12+
Lego Architecture Paris

Lego Architecture sets recreate landmarks from around the world — this one includes iconic Paris buildings like the Eiffel Tower, Louvre and Arc de Triomphe. The completed set is about 11 inches wide and eight inches tall, compact enough for desks or nightstands.
Best Lego gifts for ages 18+
Lego Ideas Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory

This detailed Lego set recreates Wonka’s chocolate factory from the 1971 movie, with a chocolate waterfall, Wonkatania boat, Willy Wonka’s office and more. It also includes nine minifigures of characters like Willy Wonka, Charlie Bucket and Augustus Gloop, to name a few.
Lego Ideas Disney Pixar Luxo Jr.

Remember the lamp bouncing on the ball at the start of every Pixar movie? That’s Luxo Jr., recreated in detail with this Lego set. The lamp has multiple hinges and joints, so you can adjust its height, swivel, tilt, rotation and positioning, and it includes a buildable ball to recreate the bounce from the short film.
Best Lego accessory gifts
Lego 4-Stud Blue Desk Drawer

Organize your Lego pieces, or anything else, using this plastic drawer in the shape of a four-studded Lego block. It stacks with other four-studded Lego storage bricks, so you can build out a drawer-system to your liking.
Lego Brick Pouch

This small, soft pouch is best for carrying non-Lego items — think school supplies, chargers, makeup, anything you might put in a small zip bag. It has one large zippered compartment and two smaller, stud-shaped ones on the top.
Lego Storage Organizer Cubes (3-Pack)

These organizer cubes can store Lego bricks or anything else that needs to be sorted and sealed. Each cube has a zipper closure and a see-through top so you can easily grab what’s inside with a quick glance. The smaller red and blue cubes fit inside the larger yellow one, if all three are empty.

title: 7 top-rated meat thermometers to end overcooked dinners
summary: Make sure your chicken, beef and pork aren’t undercooked or overcooked by using one of these top-rated meat thermometers.
story: This scenario might sound familiar. You’ve spent time in the kitchen cooking a wonderful meal. You plate everything up, but when you sit down and cut into your piece of meat, it’s totally overcooked — or, worse, raw. A meat thermometer may just be the answer to this culinary conundrum. “[Meat thermometers] let you know the internal temperature without cutting your protein open, which can dry your food out,” says Lauren Allen, chef and owner of Lauren Allen Dinners, which offers private chef experiences, virtual cooking classes and more. “That means your meat will be juicier and cooked to exactly your liking.”

Adding this kitchen gadget to your repertoire doesn’t even have to cost you much — a good one can be found for under $20, says Allen. To help you shop for one of these handy tools, I spoke with two chefs to get their advice on what to look for when choosing a meat thermometer, and then I sourced top-rated options from popular retailers like Amazon, Walmart and Target.

How to shop for a meat thermometer

There are two common types of meat thermometers intended for in-home use. Probe thermometers stay in the meat the entire time it cooks. Place your thermometer in the middle and thickest part of the protein and be sure to avoid hitting bone, says Allen. What temperature should your meat be?
Before you start cooking, it’s helpful to know the ideal temperature for whatever you are making. To help you out, the experts I spoke to recommend the following:

Chicken: Poultry needs to be cooked to at least 165 degrees Fahrenheit, both Allen and Gillepsie say. Does the type of makeup you wear determine what type of makeup remover to use?

Yes, and it’s actually one of the most overlooked parts of a typical skin care routine. “Makeup formulas behave in very different ways, so a remover that works well on a light skin tint may do very little against waterproof mascara,” says Dr. Gina Maccarone, triple board-certified cosmetic surgeon and founder of The Surgeonista. “When you match the remover to the formula, you remove makeup completely with less rubbing, and that protects the skin barrier over time.”
What type of makeup remover is best?

Turns out, there’s no one-size-fits-all makeup remover, and the type of makeup you’re wearing usually determines how you remove it. Below, I list a few popular types of makeup and the best products to remove each one based on my experts’ guidance.

Waterproof mascara and eyeliner: Waterproof makeup is hydrophobic, meaning it repels water, so water-based cleansers alone may not effectively remove it. Instead, use an oil-based or bi-phase remover to break down those water-repelling agents. “Bi-phase eye makeup remover is typically best, as it has both an oil phase and a water phase,” says Katharine Perry, board-certified nurse practitioner at MONA Dermatology. “The oil phase helps to break down the product, and the water phase helps to flush any residue.” Long-wear or matte lipstick: An oil or cleansing balm loosens long-wear lipstick much better than micellar water or a foaming cleanser, says Maccarone.Full-coverage foundation and concealer: Use a cleansing oil or balm as a first step. “These formulas often contain silicones and pigments that oil dissolves well, and massaging an oil over dry skin lifts the makeup without aggressive rubbing,” says Maccarone. Follow it up with a gentle water-based cleanser to clean your skin afterward.Tinted moisturizers and skin tints: “Lighter makeup can still have some of those staying power ingredients, so it’s best to know what is actually in your makeup when deciding on a cleanser,” says Perry. Lightweight makeup usually comes off with a gentle cleanser, but those with sunscreen might be harder to remove. “If you’re wearing sunscreen under your skin tint, which I always recommend, a quick pass with micellar water or a cleansing oil first helps make sure everything is fully removed,” says Maccarone. Liquid and cream makeup: Foundations, blushes, contours and other makeup with a cream or liquid formula, especially long-wear ones, bind more closely to the skin and usually benefit from an oil or balm first, says Maccarone. “The more a product is designed to last, the more thoughtful the removal step needs to be,” she says.Powder foundation, blush and bronzer: “Powder doesn’t have the same adherence to the skin as a liquid product would, so a gentle cleanser usually works,” says Perry.

Does removing eye makeup require special consideration?

Yes, you should be careful when removing your eye makeup. “You never want to aggressively rub your eyes because the skin around them is delicate, and too much pulling can irritate your eyes or damage your lashes,” says dermatologist and reconstructive surgeon Dr. Ariel Ostad. One trick is to soak a cotton pad with a remover and gently hold it against your closed eye for about 15 to 30 seconds, which gives the product time to loosen the makeup before you wipe it away, says Ostad.

Glitter, shimmer or highly pigmented eye makeup can be especially tricky because those tiny particles can get into your eyes. “I’d recommend using a gentle cleansing balm that’s safe for the eye area, since it can help break down stubborn makeup without a lot of rubbing,” says Ostad.
What is the difference between cleansing oils, cleansing balms and micellar water?
These are the most popular types of makeup removers, and they can have different functions depending on the type of makeup you’re using.

Cleansing oils dissolve oil-based and waterproof makeup. They usually have emulsifiers, so they turn milky and rinse away when you add water, says Maccarone. Cleansing oils are great for removing heavier makeup, especially long-wearing foundation and waterproof products.Cleansing balms do the same thing as a cleansing oil, but have a solid texture that melts when it makes contact with your skin, which many people find easier to control, says Maccarone. They’re good for stubborn makeup, including full-coverage foundation and eye makeup, says Ostad. Micellar water contains micelles, which are tiny clusters of mild cleansing molecules that attract and lift oil and makeup without needing to rinse, says Maccarone. You can usually use micellar water with a cotton pad to lift dirt, oil and makeup off your skin, says Perry. It’s usually a good choice for lighter makeup like tinted moisturizer, blush and regular mascara, and it’s convenient if you want to remove a little makeup without washing your entire face, says Ostad. However, if you’re using heavy or long-wear makeup, it might not be enough, so you should wash your face afterward.

Are makeup remover wipes actually effective?

Makeup wipes are good in a pinch and better than not washing at all, but they shouldn’t be your primary removal method. “One of the biggest issues is that they don’t always remove all the makeup, oil and dirt sitting on your skin,” says Czernik. “You also tend to rub your face more when using wipes, which can cause irritation, especially around your eyes. I’d treat them as a backup option and wash your face afterward whenever possible.”
How to choose a makeup remover based on your skin type

When choosing the right makeup remover for you, keep in mind what kind of makeup you’re using first, then narrow down your options based on your skin type. Here’s what works best for common skin types:

Dry skin: Use a cleansing balm or oil to remove makeup, which won’t strip your skin of its moisture, says Czernik.Oily or acne-prone skin: Look for a lightweight remover that rinses off easily and won’t clog your pores, says Czernik. Oily and combination skin can still use cleansing oils, ideally lightweight ones that rinse cleanly, followed by a gentle cleanser, says Maccarone.Sensitive skin: Avoid products with common irritants like fragrance or alcohols, says Czernik. Consider using a fragrance-free micellar water since that’s less likely to cause redness and irritation. Keep in mind that for more sensitive skin types (like acne-, rosacea- and eczema-prone skin), heavier makeup and oil-based cleansers may be more irritating, so consider sticking with lightweight skin tints and gentle cleansers, says Perry.

Frequently asked questions

Leftover makeup mixes with oil, sweat and debris, which can cause clogged pores, breakouts and irritation, says Maccarone. Similarly, residual mascara and liner can irritate your eyes and clog the small oil glands along the lash line. “Overnight is also when the skin does much of its repair work, and a clean surface supports that process,” says Maccarone. “One night won’t ruin your skin, but consistent, thorough removal is part of keeping it healthy over the long term.”

While some oils and balms can clog pores, this is generally a misconception. A cleansing oil is designed to emulsify and rinse off, so it shouldn’t stay on the skin long enough to clog pores, says Maccarone. “Problems tend to arise when a product contains heavier, pore-clogging oils [like cocoa butter or coconut oil], isn’t rinsed thoroughly or isn’t followed by a second cleanse,” she says. If you’re acne-prone, look for oils and balms that are noncomedogenic, meaning they won’t clog pores.

A good tip for people who are acne-prone is to double cleanse, which is when you start with an oil-based cleanser to remove makeup or sunscreen and then follow it up with a gentle water-based cleanser to remove any residue, says Perry.

For most long-wear and waterproof makeup, 20 to 30 seconds is enough. “You’ll often see the makeup begin to dissolve or transfer to the cotton pad, which is a sign it’s ready to come off with minimal effort,” says Maccarone. “If something is particularly stubborn, a second application is gentler than more force.”
You should always avoid harsh fragrances and alcohols when you can, as well as acids and abrasive formulas like scrubs, experts say.
Below are some of the biggest mistakes people make when removing their makeup, according to my experts:

Rubbing too hard. “Friction irritates the skin, can contribute to redness and breakouts, and over the years, stresses the delicate skin around the eyes,” says Maccarone. “Removal should be intentional and gentle, never rushed.”

Rubbing too hard. “Friction irritates the skin, can contribute to redness and breakouts, and over the years, stresses the delicate skin around the eyes,” says Maccarone. “Removal should be intentional and gentle, never rushed.”
Over-cleansing, especially to the point where the skin feels tight afterwards, which can strip skin of its natural moisture and cause irritation, says Perry.

Not taking enough time to remove all makeup. If there’s makeup left behind, it can lead to clogged pores, breakouts and skin irritation. “I always recommend washing your face afterward,” says Czernik.

A good way to check is to take a clean, damp cotton pad and gently wipe it across your face after cleansing. “If you’re still seeing foundation or other makeup coming off, you haven’t removed everything,” says Czernik. “I would pay extra attention to your hairline, around your nose and under your eyes; those are areas people tend to miss without realizing it.”
