title: Rep. Ro Khanna allies launch a draft campaign for the 2028 presidential race
summary: Exclusive: The California congressman has been traveling the country and building prominence among progressives.
story: Allies of Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., are launching an effort to lay groundwork for him to run for president, the leaders of a new draft committee told NBC News.

Former Rep. Jamaal Bowman, D-N.Y., and progressive strategist Nomiki Konst are co-chairs of the group — “Run Ro” — which can raise money from donors and begin building support for a Khanna candidacy while he continues to weigh a 2028 bid.

The move comes in the immediate aftermath of a midterm election in which voters swept Democrats into power in the House and the Senate, with some high-profile progressives among the big winners. It also comes as the party’s left wing looks for a new champion who can run in the progressive lane that Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., occupied in the 2016 and 2020 presidential nominating contests.
“By launching now, we are trying to ensure that the presidential primary debate is framed from a progressive populist perspective,” Konst said.
The challenges facing a possible Khanna candidacy are immense. Only one person was ever elected to the presidency directly from the House: James Garfield, R-Ohio, in 1880.

Khanna, a fifth-term lawmaker, has made headlines with bipartisan efforts to force the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files and to end the war in Iran. He is nonetheless not even the most famous House progressive considering a presidential bid.
That unofficial title belongs to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., who hasn’t yet said whether she will seek the presidency, run for a Senate seat in New York or remain in the House.

“She is my sister, and I love her,” Bowman said of Ocasio-Cortez, with whom he shared a close alliance in the House. “Ro Khanna has shown the work ethic, the humility and the vision that we need in this moment.”

Khanna, who was a co-chair of Sanders’ 2020 campaign, is also a favorite of progressives around the country. And he has been traveling to early primary states for months. He makes no effort to hide his presidential ambitions, and many of his colleagues believe he will jump into the race.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
He welcomed the draft committee in a statement to NBC News.

“I’m honored that people are encouraging me to run on a platform of Medicare for All, ending foreign wars and taxing the billionaires,” he said. “We need America’s Next New Deal. Whether I run or support someone else is something I will decide with my family after the holidays.”
Konst said the draft committee will allow her and Bowman to organize now so Khanna isn’t late to the game if he does run.

“The centrists organize and strategize early,” she said. “They have their donors, corporate consultants and leaders lined up for years. Building off the lessons of past primaries, our goal is to channel the progressive energy into a vessel for organizing and spreading our winning message early, as we can’t wait for the politics to line up.”
No candidate has yet entered the field for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination.

title: Trump brags about the White House ballroom in his first post-election appearance
summary: One day after elections in which Democrats took back the House and the Senate, the president addressed workers building the White House ballroom and said he didn’t regret starting the Iran war.
story: In his first public appearance since Republicans racked up major losses in the midterm elections, President Donald Trump boasted Wednesday about the White House ballroom under construction and largely skirted talk about his party’s performance.

“This is a special structure. It’s going to be not only one of the biggest, but it’ll be the most beautiful ballroom, I think, anywhere in the world, and they’ve been trying to get it for 150 years,” Trump told construction workers at the ballroom site on the White House grounds, where the East Wing previously stood.

“This will be something very special. And so we’re putting up the last piece of steel. I thought it would be appropriate to have the media here,” he added, hinting that the ballroom’s “official opening” would be in the near future.

The president’s only remarks on the election results — which saw Democrats regain control of both houses of Congress, notching wins in longtime GOP strongholds like Texas — came in response to questions from the media after his remarks.

When asked to weigh in on the race to pick a new House Republican leader in light of Speaker Mike Johnson’s decision not to run again, Trump said, “We’ll stay out of it.” He said he did not ask Johnson to step down.

Asked for comment on Vice President JD Vance’s statement that Republicans lost the election because of the war on Iran, Trump said, “I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term.” He added: “At the same time, if I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again because long term it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.”
The president signed a steel beam destined for the ballroom project, adorned with two gold presidential seals, and addressed criticism that he is too focused on White House renovations.
For Subscribers

“I’m doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol of America and it’s got to be pristine — it’s got to be perfect,” he said. “And if you take a look at it, that’s what it is right now. You have no idea how much work we had to do.”
For Subscribers
Trump claimed that it was “the dream of presidents to have a ballroom for 150 years” and bragged about the “most beautiful marble” in the ballroom.
“I got it for the floor of the ballroom at the White House. And it’s going to be beautiful. The walls are going to be very — you’ll see a lot of glass,” he said.

Trump first announced plans for the ballroom in July 2025 and has frequently spoken about it during official White House events on unrelated subjects and at campaign rallies. The project has faced legal obstacles, though the Supreme Court said in late August that construction could proceed indefinitely.

On Monday, Trump spent most of his final pre-election speech in front of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool touting the renovations he ordered around Washington, D.C., with very little time devoted to the midterms.

title: Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia, alleging defamation over Epstein comments
summary: Garcia is poised to be the next chair of the House Oversight Committee, which has subpoenaed Black as part of its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein.
story: Billionaire Leon Black filed a defamation lawsuit Wednesday against Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, which has spearheaded a Jeffrey Epstein investigation.
Black has been the target of subpoenas from the Republican-led committee, which unanimously voted in September to hold him in contempt over his refusal to comply with those subpoenas.

Black, a former Wall Street private equity investor who had a business relationship with Epstein, sued Garcia in the Southern District of New York, alleging he “has knowingly and willfully lied about Leon Black and defamed him.” The suit cites comments from Garcia that Black was “at the center” and “directly involved” with Epstein’s crimes.

A spokesperson for Garcia didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit. Garcia said in a statement in September in response to a lawsuit Black filed against the committee that Black had “funded Epstein’s abuse and trafficking of women,” adding: “Multiple women have also accused Black of sexual assault. His connections to Epstein and his unwillingness to cooperate are unacceptable.”

In a statement about the lawsuit against Garcia on Wednesday, a spokesperson for Black wrote that “he has never abused a woman; he has never been with an underage woman; he has never been involved with sex trafficking; and, he never paid Epstein for women.”
With Democrats set to take control of the House in January, Garcia is poised to become the new chair of the Oversight Committee.

Black stepped down from the hedge fund he co-founded, Apollo Global Management, in 2021 after the firm conducted an independent review of his ties to Epstein. The review found that Black, who has denied wrongdoing tied to Epstein, wasn’t involved in Epstein’s criminal activities.

Black sat for a voluntary closed-door transcribed interview with the House Oversight Committee over the summer but left before it was over. Lawmakers on the committee issued subpoenas to compel him to answer questions they said he wasn’t answering, but Black didn’t show up for a later deposition. He then sued the committee to block the subpoenas for his appearance and nondisclosure agreements tied to Epstein. The case is still being litigated.

The House later voted to hold Black in contempt of Congress. Reuters reported that the Justice Department said Sept. 16 in a statement that the “US Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia will review the referral of Mr. Black carefully and will not hesitate to pursue additional cases where the evidence supports.”
No charges have been filed against Black.

title: ‘A Watergate-level repudiation’: Ted Cruz weighs in on midterm wave
summary: Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, urged his party to prioritize pocketbook issues after Democrats swept elections across the state.
story: Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Wednesday described the historic Democratic sweep in the midterm elections as an “ass-kicking” for Republicans, urging the party to deliver on economic promises in the next cycle.
“It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election, it was a Watergate-level repudiation,” Cruz said on an episode of his podcast, describing the Democratic shift across the country as a “blue tsunami.”
Cruz, who is not up for re-election until 2030, said that “understandably, people were pissed off,” as “Republicans didn’t do enough to address their very real pain.”
He pointed to tariffs’ raising costs and the Iran war’s dragging on for “too long,” adding, “Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.”
“Too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care,” he said.
NBC News exit polls found that more than 80% of voters said they were worried about the prices of necessities: gas and diesel fuel, food and groceries, utilities and healthcare.
“We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people’s lives, and we need to deal with the consequences,” Cruz said.
Cruz said he did call his new colleague, Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico, to congratulate him on his victory.
“I will work with Democrats when they’re willing to be reasonable,” he said. “It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.”
However, he also said, “Texas will be red again.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain’t us. Texas is still Texas,” Cruz said. “We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives.”

In his own analysis of the elections, Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, who lost the GOP Senate primary in May to state Attorney General Ken Paxton, also acknowledged Republicans’ shortcomings on the economy.
In 2024, voters “trusted Mr. Trump and the Republicans over Kamala Harris and the Democrats to protect their pocketbooks,” Cornyn wrote in an op-ed published by The Wall Street Journal.
However, Cornyn also argued that the party “forgot” how to win elections and instead favored “performative politics.”

“When Republicans force voters to choose between policy and personal character, it is unfair to them and suicidal for us,” he wrote. “We know what the American people want because they showed us: a big-tent Republican Party, competent, focused on Americans’ daily concerns, with room for traditional conservatives and MAGA supporters alike.”
Cornyn wrote that “anyone who is willing to turn the page, restore integrity and rebuild our party can count me in.”

Democrats prevailed across the state Tuesday, with Talarico ending 38 years of GOP dominance over the Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa making history as Texas’ first Latina governor and the first Democratic governor in over three decades.

title: 5 key insights from the NBC News Exit Poll about the blue tsunami
summary: Voters expressed feeling fed up with the economy; Democratic candidates emerged more well-liked, and Trump was resoundingly rejected.
story: It was a historic blue tsunami: The Democratic Party captured both chambers of Congress, flipping as many as seven seats in the Senate and at least 29 in the House of Representatives.
Just two years ago, the nation had been hit by a red wave. How did things turn around so dramatically?

A cocktail of crucial factors: Voters feeling fed up with the economy, Democratic candidates emerging as more well-liked, important voting blocs — including Latinos and Black men — shifting blue, opinions about the Republican Party dropping and a resounding rejection of President Donald Trump himself, according to the NBC News Exit Poll.
Here are five key insights we have gleaned about Tuesday’s stunning midterms analyzing data from the poll, which surveyed more than 79,000 voters nationwide.
Follow live updates on the midterm elections
1) Americans were deeply negative on the state of the economy and gloomy about the future of the country.
An overwhelming majority of voters (75%) rated the nation’s economy as “not so good” or “poor,” the poll showed. And they soured on their trust in Republicans to handle it.

Sixty-nine percent said the U.S. economic system favors the wealthy, and only 31% said it favors most Americans. This perception came at a time when the vast majority of voters expressed concerns about the cost of living. More than 80% of voters said they were worried about the price of necessities: gas and diesel fuel, food and groceries, utilities and healthcare.

Thirty-seven percent of voters said they favored Republican control of the economy, while 43% favored Democrats — a flip in perspective from the 2024 election. Voters also blamed Trump: 65% said the president’s policies had made the economy worse. Just 27% said they had made the economy better.
Sixty-two percent said higher-than-usual prices are more because of Trump’s policies than factors outside his control, and 65% said his tariff policies hurt the national economy.

Their frustration extended beyond the economy — and into a pessimistic view of the U.S. overall. Three in four voters said they were unhappy with how things are going in the U.S., and more than a third (38%) said they were angry about the state of the country.
More than half of voters (57%) said that life for the next generation of Americans will be worse than today; just 22% said they believed it would be better.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
2) Democratic candidates enjoyed advantages on favorability, character and experience.

In an overwhelmingly negative political environment, Democratic Senate candidates emerged as well-liked in races that looked tough for them at the beginning of the election cycle, according to the poll.

Democrats above water on favorability included Jon Ossoff in Georgia, where a remarkable 59% of state voters said they viewed him favorably; James Talarico in Texas, where 52% of voters said they viewed him positively; and Josh Turek in Iowa, where 49% of voters said they viewed him favorably. All three candidates won their races.
Republicans, meanwhile, struggled to win over voters.
In two key Senate races, voters expressed negative opinions about Republican candidates’ personal character.

In Kansas, 43% of voters said Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, an OB-GYN who faced scrutiny after The New York Times reported that he sued hundreds of patients over unpaid bills, had the right character for the job. Marshall has described the story as a “hit job.”

Voter opinions were worse about Ken Paxton’s personal character. Only 34% of Texas voters thought positively of the attorney general, who has battled scandals for years and was impeached in 2023 by the Republican-controlled state House before the state Senate acquitted him.
Both Paxton and Marshall lost their Senate bids.

Candidates aligned with Trump also struggled. In North Carolina, Michael Whatley was seen as too supportive of Trump (60%), and in South Carolina, where the president endorsed Darline Graham, only 35% of voters said she had the right experience.
3) After flirting with the GOP in 2024, big Democratic voting blocs swung back with a vengeance.
By ignoring or denigrating many of the new voters who were key to Trump’s victory two years ago, Republicans squandered the opportunity to cement a new coalition of voters.
Latinos, who notably gave Trump almost half (46%) of their votes in 2024, bounced back to the Democrats, who garnered 62% of Latino support in races for the House, the poll showed.
Among Black male voters, 1 in 5 went for Trump in 2024. That share shrank to 13% for Republican House candidates this year.

Trump narrowly won men under age 25 in 2024, getting 49% of their votes compared to 48% for Democrat Kamala Harris. But young men swung dramatically away from the GOP in House races this year: Democrats swept them by a 68% to 28% margin.
On the whole, more Trump voters had buyer’s remorse (6% supported Democratic House candidates) than Harris voters (3% defected to the GOP).
4) And Trump himself was soundly rejected by voters.
Trump tried to energize his base by encouraging his supporters to vote like, “I’m on the ballot.” But the nation had largely soured on his presidency, according to the poll.
Trump’s approval rating among voters, just 38%, was the lowest Election Day rating for any president since 2008.
Forty-three percent of voters said they cast their House ballot to express opposition to Trump. Just 16% said they voted to express support for him.

Voters gave Trump overwhelmingly negative marks on key aspects of his presidency, saying that he prioritizes “his own personal interests” over the country’s (62%), that his war against Iran was the “wrong decision” (63%) and that his immigration actions had “gone too far” (57%).
5) A key distinction: It’s a blue tsunami, not a progressive earthquake.
Politicians and pundits alike mistook Trump’s 2024 victory as an endorsement of his deeply conservative plans. But the 2024 NBC Exit Poll found little evidence of an ideological shift to the right.
The story is the same this year: On key issues, voters are no more progressive than they were two years ago.
Among voters this year, 64% said abortion should be legal in most or all cases. That’s just a notch below the share of 65% in 2024.

Twenty-three percent of the electorate considered themselves liberal in 2024, while 35% called themselves conservative. Those numbers hardly budged among voters in 2026, standing at 25% liberal, 34% conservative.

Voters’ opinions of socialism remained largely negative, at 54% unfavorable and 33% favorable. Just 1 in 5 voters this year considered themselves democratic socialists. By contrast, capitalism remains relatively well-regarded in the minds of voters (57% favorable, 32% unfavorable).

title: Indiana executes prisoner despite lawyers’ concerns over state’s lethal drug supplier
summary: Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, was executed by lethal injection for the 2010 murders of two young children in his care.
story: Indiana carried out its first execution of the year early Thursday after lawyers for the condemned man failed in their bid to stop it, despite new details emerging about the state’s secretive process of obtaining lethal injection drugs.

Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, was put to death at Indiana State Prison shortly after midnight for the 2010 murders of two young children in a house fire, state officials said. He had no last words and was pronounced dead 45 minutes later.
The state does not generally allow media witnesses to attend, and Weisheit’s legal team could not immediately be reached for comment about his execution.

The race to spare his life had ended up before the Indiana Supreme Court late Wednesday, when the state’s highest court voted 3-2 to allow the execution to proceed. The dissenting justices would have permitted temporarily pausing the execution for 10 days to sort out questions over the lethal drugs.
After the execution, Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita said the state was delivering “long-awaited justice” for victims Alyssa Lynch, 8, and her brother, Caleb, 5.
“This case stands as a clear affirmation that those who commit the most heinous crimes against the most vulnerable will be held fully accountable under Indiana law,” Rokita said in a statement.
Weisheit’s execution is one of three nationally set for Thursday, with the others to be carried out by lethal injection in Alabama and Florida.

In the hours before the execution, attorneys for Weisheit had called on Indiana Gov. Mike Braun to halt his lethal injection execution and order an independent review of the state’s procedures over allegations that the state obtained its chemicals from a pharmacy currently on probation and facing suspension of its license.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“Laid bare, the apparent conduct here is patently unworthy of the public’s confidence in the solemn exercise of state power in taking a human being’s life in the name of the people,” Joe Perkovich, an attorney for Weisheit, said in a statement Wednesday.

Weisheit did not contest his guilt but sought Braun to commute his sentence to life in prison without parole. His attorneys had cited Tennessee’s failed lethal injection execution of Christa Pike on Sept. 30 in his new application to the governor seeking a reprieve, saying Indiana’s protocol is “more susceptible to catastrophic failures such as the one that placed Ms. Pike in a coma,” and that the pharmacy listed on a state Department of Correction invoice has a history of “rampant mishandling of drugs.”
Pharmacy inspected

An updated inventory log provided to NBC News showed that the Department of Correction added six vials of the lethal drug, pentobarbital, to the prison supply on Oct. 29. An invoice included in the reprieve application says that the state paid $275,000 for those vials — far higher than the typical $15,120 to $16,250 price for commercially made injectable pentobarbital. The invoice is heavily redacted and shows neither the date nor supplier for the transaction.

Indiana law shields the identities of participants, pharmacies and suppliers involved in carrying out executions. However, a September 2025 invoice for the same dollar amount that corresponds with the last time the state added vials of pentobarbital to its supply accidentally revealed the possible supplier of the drug, according to exhibits included in Weisheit’s application for a reprieve.
The exhibits were produced by the Department of Correction in response to a records request related to Weisheit’s execution date.
An address retrievable from beneath a black redaction corresponds to the address for Pharmaneek, an Indianapolis-based pharmacy.

Pharmaneek is scheduled to appear before the Indiana Board of Pharmacy on Monday — four days after Weisheit’s execution — over allegations that the pharmacy violated its probation after failed inspections by the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency and the Food and Drug Administration.

The inspections found that Pharmaneek stored drugs in unlabeled bottles, found bottles of expired drugs “on random inspection of active pharmacy shelves” and failed to keep consistent temperature logs for pharmacy storage areas. In a settlement agreement with the state, Pharmaneek said some inspection problems were due to remodeling.
According to an FDA inspection report from March 2026, the “facility is not maintained in a good state of repair, creating unsanitary conditions whereby drug products may be contaminated with filth.”
The FDA report says its findings do not represent a final agency determination of compliance.

Indiana licensing records for Pharmaneek that correspond with details listed on the Department of Correction invoice show that the pharmacy’s license and controlled substance registration are on probation.

According to a legal filing dated Sept. 24, the Indiana Board of Pharmacy, which investigates complaints and can issue penalties, ordered Pharmaneek to appear before its members on Oct. 5 to “show cause” why its pharmacy license “should not be suspended on an emergency basis or subjected to the imposition of further sanctions.”
A motion from Pharmaneek’s legal counsel included in the reprieve application shows that a lawyer for the pharmacy asked that the appearance be moved to Monday.
Pharmaneek did not respond to NBC News’ multiple requests for comment this week by phone. The Indiana Department of Correction also did not respond to requests for comment or an interview.
The governor’s office declined to comment Wednesday on the allegations that the Department of Correction obtained execution drugs from a pharmacy on probation.

While Pharmaneek is currently barred from mixing custom drugs — a process known as compounding — Weisheit’s reprieve application alleges the pharmacy is acting as a middleman for the Department of Correction, supplying it with manufactured pentobarbital the department is not permitted to purchase straight from traditional drug manufacturers.

In court filings prior to the execution of Roy Lee Ward in October 2025, the state said the pentobarbital it planned to use was produced by a pharmaceutical company instead of a compounding pharmacy, and distributed “without any post-manufacturing customizations.”
Major drug companies have explicitly warned states not to use their drugs for executions and have sued states for the return of their chemicals.

Sagent Pharmaceuticals, one of two pharmaceutical companies that manufacture pentobarbital in the United States, did not respond to emailed questions about whether it has a relationship with Pharmaneek; however, the company’s policies do not allow its distributors or wholesalers to sell its products to prisons for use in lethal injection. The other, the drugmaker Hikma, said the company does not have a purchase agreement with Pharmaneek.
“We have strict prohibitions and controls intended to prevent the use of our medicines in capital punishment,” said Steven Weiss, a Hikma representative.

A spokesperson for Rokita told NBC News his office is “confident in the ability to safely and lawfully carry out the scheduled execution.” They added that Weisheit’s lawyers “have publicly identified a pharmacy that they claim is connected to Indiana’s execution-drug supply, despite state law requiring supplier information to remain confidential.”
Clemency denied

Weisheit had been on death row for 13 years after a Vanderburgh County jury convicted him of murdering Alyssa Lynch and her younger brother, Caleb, the children of his then-girlfriend, Lisa Lynch. She had been at work while Weisheit was watching the children in their Evansville home.

Prosecutors said Weisheit bound and gagged Caleb, then placed railroad flares in his clothing and near his body before setting fire to the home and fleeing out of state. Alyssa’s body was found in a closet. The children had died of smoke inhalation.
Weisheit appealed his conviction, including on the grounds of ineffective counsel, but was denied relief.

Last month, Weisheit appeared at a clemency hearing in front of the state parole board, during which his mental illness and other health struggles were discussed. He was unable to offer a reason for why he killed the Lynch children.
“There is no excuse or explanation for what I did,” Weisheit said.
Lisa Lynch asked the board to uphold his death sentence and keep the focus on her children.
“Every birthday, every holiday, every landmark moment is marked by their agonizing absence,” she said. “Time passes, but the weight of losing them never fades.”

The children’s father, Steven Lynch, told the board that he supported clemency and forgave Weisheit for his actions. The board ultimately recommended Braun deny clemency, which he agreed Monday not to grant.

Lisa Lynch could not be reached for comment ahead of Weisheit’s scheduled execution. Steven Lynch told NBC News that he had hoped Weisheit could be shown mercy and said he was thinking of the convicted killer’s family as they brace for a finite loss like the one he experienced when his own children were murdered.
“No parent should have to outlive their child,” Steven Lynch said before the execution, adding that “mercy is extended to even the least of us.”

title: 2 children and father fall to deaths in Pennsylvania in apparent murder-suicide
summary: The bodies of Patrick Lynch and his children, 6 and 8 years old, were found near a parking garage behind the Municipal Building in Mt. Lebanon.
story: A Pennsylvania dad and his two children fell to their deaths on Election Day in what police suspect was a double murder-suicide.
Their bodies were found a little after 4 p.m. Tuesday behind the Mt. Lebanon Municipal Building and near a neighboring parking garage, Allegheny County police said in a statement.

“When first responders arrived on scene, they found an adult male and two children suffering injuries from an apparent fall,” police said. “First responders attempted life saving measures until medical professionals pronounced the three deceased on scene.”
The Allegheny County Medical Examiner’s Office identified the dead as Patrick Lynch, 42; James Lynch, 8; and Caroline Lynch, 6. All three lived in Mt. Lebanon.
“Preliminary information suggests that this incident is a murder-suicide and there is no danger to the community,” police said.
Mt. Lebanon Police Chief Jason Haberman said at a news conference Tuesday, “We’re treating this incident not as an accident.”
For Subscribers

“There will be a significant amount of trauma associated with this event for the community,” he said. “Our condolences to everybody involved. ... Everyone in the Mt. Lebanon community will know someone involved in this incident.”
For Subscribers
Investigators have not divulged any details about what may have led to the deaths.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7, to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Al Roker Preps for His Memorable ‘Seinfeld’ Cameo in 1993
summary: See Al Roker prepare for his cameo on “Seinfeld” in 1993.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Al Roker on Dec. 5, 1993, preparing for his classic cameo on “Seinfeld.”
Al Roker is synonymous with TODAY, but he also lent his talents to another NBC series during its heyday.
Yes, Al famously appeared as himself on an episode of “Seinfeld” that aired during the sitcom’s fifth season on Dec. 9, 1993.
A few days before that, though, on Dec. 5, Al took TODAY viewers behind the scenes for his cameo.
What Advice Did Al Get From ‘Seinfeld’ Star Jerry Seinfeld?
“It’s my big break, my acting debut, a shot at stardom,” Al joked in a voiceover as he walked onto the “Seinfeld” set.
Al then chatted up the cast to get some tips on how he should approach his role.
“It’s really just pretending,” “Seinfeld” star and creator Jerry Seinfeld told him.
Jason Alexander Shared a Different Perspective
Co-star Jason Alexander had a more dire take on the matter.

“One thought that should be going through your head at all times is, ‘Please, God, don’t let me screw it up,’” he said matter of factly. “If you take all the acting training that I’ve had and you distill it down to that, that’s basically what I do.”

Alexander took it a step further by also encouraging Al to play “who passed wind” if the camera lingers on him when the scene ends. He showed what that kind of facial expression looks like and how effective it can be.
“It’s good for any situation. It covers everything,” he said.
Did Al Win Over the ‘Seinfeld’ Cast?

In the episode, Al, appearing on the cover of TV Guide, becomes a key cog in the plot. The segment captured Al rehearsing his big scene, which took place on a New York City subway. Co-star Julia Louis-Dreyfus was not impressed when he later asked her if he had potential.
“No, I don’t, Al,” she quipped. “You’re talentless, Al.”
Al was surprised to learn the cast doesn’t get nervous, but he powered through, regardless, and got a nice round of applause from the audience when Seinfeld introduced him after the shoot.

title: Charles Leclerc and Alexandra Welcome First Baby Together. Find Out Her Adorable Name
summary: Formula One and Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc and wife Alexandra announced the arrival of their first child together on Nov. 4.
story: Say hello to baby Leclerc.
Formula One and Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc and wife Alexandra announced the arrival of their first child together on Nov. 4.
The couple shared a photo of their daughter’s little legs in a pink onesie and tiny feet in light rose-colored booties on their Instagram. In the caption, they shared her name and date of birth.
“Bianca 🤍 3.11.26,” they wrote, sharing her Nov. 3 arrival. Baby Bianca Leclerc joins the couple’s beloved dog Leo.
Charles Leclerc’s fellow F1 drivers congratulated the couple, with Carlos Sainz writing, “So happy for you 😊 Welcome to the world Bianca.”
Newly-crowned F1 champion Kimi Antonelli also commented, “Congratulazioni! ❤️,” while George Russell and Oscar Piastri both wrote, “Congrats to you both!”
The official account for the F1 Academy, the female-led Formula 4 league, also added, “Congratulations! Maybe we’ll see her on the grid in the future…”
Charles Leclerc’s brother, Arthur, also left three red heart emoji, while Eva Longoria and Nina Dobrev also congratulated the new parents.
The new mom first showed off her baby bump in an August Instagram post. She then continued to show off her fashionable pregnancy style on her social media and at races around the world.

Their baby girl’s arrival comes a year after the couple announced their engagement on Nov. 2, 2025. Charles and Alexandra would go on to get married on Feb. 28, 2026, according to the athlete’s Instagram. Their civil ceremony was held in Monte Carlo, Monaco.

“A day we’ll forever remember. Part one is done and part 2 will be next year with all of our close ones,” Charles Leclerc captioned his Instagram post, which included stunning photos from their celebration.
It’s still a busy time for the F1 driver, who will next race on Nov. 8 at the Brazilian Grand Prix followed by the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Nov. 21.

title: Bob Dylan Met Pope Leo and the Internet Can’t Get Over the Rocker’s Outfit
summary: Bobby D. got dressed in his Sunday best to meet Pope Leo XIV. And his look has people talking.
story: Bobby D. got dressed in his Sunday best to meet Pope Leo XIV.
The official Instagram account of the Vatican shared a photo of legendary musician Bob Dylan and the pope, who met in a “private audience” on Nov. 4.

And while the meeting of the two high-profile figures alone was enough to grab the attention of fans, it was really Dylan’s ensemble — a pitch-black hoodie, paired with an equally dark-colored jacket and pants — that stole the show.
“Dylan innovating again by being the first person ever to great a Pope with the hood on,” one person wrote on Instagram of the look.
Dylan had swung by the pope’s official residence, the Vatican’s Apostolic Palace, amid his Italy concert dates on his worldwide “Rough and Rowdy Ways Tour.”
According to the Vatican, the pope presented the Nobel Prize-winning musician with a rosary and Dylan returned the gesture by gifting Pope Leo a copy of his autobiography, “Chronicles: Volume One.”
Most of the internet, however, appeared to be hung up on Dylan’s hooded outfit.
“Why is bob Dylan dressed like the grim reaper 😂” one fan wrote on Instagram.
Several others made comparisons between Dylan and the famous hooded “Star Wars” villain, Emperor Palpatine.
“At first glance i thought it was Palpatine,” another commenter wrote.
It appears that the pope has been a fan of Dylan’s for some time. In fact, he quoted the artist in his book “Disarmed and Disarming: Peace Is a Gift,” released in July.
The book’s forward references lyrics from Dylan’s unpublished 1963 song “Go Away You Bomb.”
The visit marks the second meeting between Dylan and a sitting Pope.

The musician met with Pope John Paul II in 1997 when he performed at the 23rd National Eucharistic Congress in Bologna along with several other artists, the Vatican points out. Pope John Paul II gave a nod to Dylan in his speech to the youth at the event, quoting the artist’s 1963 song “Blowin’ in the Wind.”

title: Steve Kornacki Reveals Why He Abruptly Left His Election Day Livestream After 10 Hours
summary: Steve Kornacki shares why he abruptly ended his election day livestream after 10 hours, as well as thanked viewers for tuning in.
story: We’re all human, including — believe it or not — the almost infatigable Steve Kornacki.
The NBC News chief data analyst on Nov. 4 revealed on social media platform X why he abruptly left his election night livestream, better known as the “Kornacki Cam,” without closing out the show.

Around the 10 hour mark of his livestream, Kornacki had told viewers that he was taking a quick five-minute break and that he would “be right back.” However, the beloved NBC stats pro did not return. And it turns out, the marathon of election coverage really took a toll on Kornacki.

“I was sure 13 hours would be fine but things caught up to me in a hurry at hour 10. I can’t say thanks enough to all of you,” the data analyst wrote on X. “What a ride and I think we did make livestream history. Sorry for the abrupt ending.”

Kornacki, who’s been praised for his mental fortitude, particularly on election nights past, was met with an overwhelming of not only understanding from viewers, but also praise for his work in breaking down the high-stakes races for such long hours.
“10 hours. Not including commuting in, and prep. Probably 12 hours,” one viewer wrote on Instagram. “My guy, go home and recharge till Thursday, we good! Oh and THANK YOU!!”
Another commenter called Kornacki a “legend.”
“I was locked in the whole time on the Kornacki cam,” the social media user wrote. “Go take a long nap my guy, you’ve earned it.”

Kornacki has long been a staple on election nights, giving NBC News viewers a look at key races, polling and results. His work on election night has even earned him the nickname “Map Daddy” and “Chart Throb.”

The data analyst’s “Kornacki Cam” this year, streamed from 30 Rockefeller Plaza, was particularly successful. The 10-hour livestream drew more than 6.3 million views on YouTube alone. Across all platforms, the program garnered a record of 29 million views, making it the top election livestream for the midterms.
Take a bow, Steve. You’ve more than earned it!

title: Viral Kid Podcasters Hen-Dawg and Jimmy V React to a Surprise from TODAY Anchors, and You Have to See Their Faces
summary: They’ve interviewed an NFL Hall of Famer and gotten an autograph from Chicago Bears star Caleb Williams, but kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg were left speechless by a surprise on TODAY.
story: They’ve interviewed an NFL Hall of Famer and gotten an autograph from Chicago Bears star Caleb Williams, but kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg were left speechless by a surprise on TODAY.

Henry “Hen-Dawg” Zotti and Jimmy “V” Maley, both 10, are diehard Chicago Bears fans, the middle school heirs to the iconic Bill Swerski’s Superfans on “Saturday Night Live” in their love for Da Bears.
Despite their devotion to the black and orange, Hen-Dawg had never even been to a Bears game — until now.

The boys were surprised by Craig Melvin, Savannah Guthrie and Carson Daly during a video call on TODAY Nov. 4 when they were gifted tickets to the Bears’ Sunday Night Football game on Nov. 8 against the visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Hen-Dawg’s face went blank in disbelief as the surprise started to sink in. Jimmy V’s mother then entered the room with two tickets for the boys, who yelled in delight before sharing a delirious hug.
“Thank you so much!” Jimmy V said.
“We’re going to kill ‘em this weekend!” Hen-Dawg said.

The boys will surely have some fresh content for their podcast after their trip to Chicago’s legendary Soldier Field. They already have interviewed Hall of Famer former Bears linebacker Brian Urlacher and received a signed copy of the Madden 27 video game from current Bears star quarterback Caleb Williams.
Hen-Dawg also dressed as Williams for Halloween this year.
“He has the most aura,” he said.
The tandem made their TODAY debut in September, becoming instant fan favorites with their straight talk. They also have become mini celebrities at school.
“The older kids that have phones usually ask for pictures,” Jimmy V said.

It’s not easy to knock them off their game like Savannah, Craig and Carson did with their surprise, considering they don’t get starstruck. Urlacher is one of the greatest linebackers in NFL history and a Bears icon, but they talked to him like anybody else.
“Just another podcast with another person,” Jimmy V said. “Just talking to a first-ballot Hall of Famer, nothing much.”

They also have plenty to discuss this year, as the Bears are off to a 6-2 start. They recently traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and just walloped the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday Night Football.

The way the Bears have been playing has the boys thinking this is the year they will finally win their first Super Bowl since their legendary 1985 team. They believe Chicago will do it in honor of franchise legend Mike Ditka, a Hall of Fame Bears player and coach who died at 86 on Oct. 9.
“Mike Ditka from the stars is going to to watch us win it all,” Jimmy V said.

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Season 11 Finale Recap: Who Gets Married and Who Splits Up?
summary: Who gets married and who splits up on Love Is Blind Season 11 finale which aired on November 4?
story: Warning: Spoilers from Season 11 of “Love Is blind” below…
After a promising start, Season 11 of “Love Is Blind” has gone off the rails, setting the stage for an unpredictable finale.

Six Boston couples got engaged in the pods when the season premiered on Oct. 14. But only five moved onto the next stage of the experiment after Scott “Stew” Stewart and Jacqueline “Jax” Guelli swiftly called it quits following their first meeting. Then, in the group of episodes released prior to the finale, former fan-favorite couple Rob Feeley and Michaella Giorgio broke up after he began to spiral and question the authenticity of their relationship.

When Episode 12, out Nov. 4, started, only four couples remained, but that didn’t last long. Two more pairs decided to go their separate ways before the big day. So, only two couples made it to the end of the experiment and their wedding day, where they announced in front of their friends and family if they wanted to say “I do.”
Read a recap of how the season ended for each couple, below, and find out what fans can expect from the emotional reunion.
Did Erika Ellis and Blake Carver Get Married?

The finale opens with Erika Ellis and Blake Carver continuing their conversation from the previous episode. Erika is uncertain that they can merge their different lifestyles. She tells Blake that she isn’t interested in living on a boat or being in a constant state of “limbo.” He says that he wants her to follow her heart and hopes that it leads her to him. But he also says he doesn’t want her to feel “hostage” in their relationship if he has to travel for months.
“I think at this point there’s too many concerns, too many questions, that I can’t say ‘yes’ at the altar,” Erika says. She adds that the best decision would be for them to leave the experiment.

While processing the breakup, Blake has a different demeanor. He agrees that they needed to end their relationship, but he refuses to tell producers if the love he felt for Erika is a feeling he has never felt before. He also says he feels “relieved” and “exhausted” after their split.
When a producer asks about Blake being emotional, he replies, “Erika cried. I didn’t cry. Who said I cried?” before laughing.
Meanwhile, Erika says her heart is “heavy” and she is feeling a “swirl of emotions.”
She reveals that she did want to have a wedding and possibly marry Blake. “It’ll be OK,” she tells herself as she wipes away tears.
Did Wilnie Louis and Wilson Monteiro Get Married?

Both Wilnie Louis and Wilson Monteiro are shown enjoying their respective bachelorette and bachelor parties with the other engaged couples. Wilnie seems eager to walk down the aisle and marry Wilson. But he appears to have doubts, looking uninterested as his friends question him about the upcoming wedding ceremony.
After the parties, the show cuts to Wilson arriving at Wilnie’s house. He explains that he wanted to “link up again today given our last conversation.”

He begins to list a series of complaints about how much Wilnie is contributing to the household regarding cooking and cleaning. She pushes back and says she isn’t messy. She also mentions occasions when she has cooked for them.
“I think I realized that I just thrive in an environment where the energy is high,” Wilson says.

Wilnie defends herself again, explaining that she does bring positive energy to their relationship but it is difficult when she works long days. She then points out that she has had to affirm Wilson often and she doesn’t feel like he does the same for her.
“I don’t think you like me,” she says, revealing that she has been thinking he would reject her at the altar.

After Wilson says they shouldn’t get married, Wilnie becomes emotional. She says she has given him more grace than he has given her. While talking to producers, Wilnie sheds more tears. She says Wilson’s comments felt like he was attacking her as a woman and person and it wasn’t “fair.”
“I just feel like those were such horrible things to say,” she says.
“He expected me to be more like his mom,” she later adds. “My mom did not come to America and work this hard for my identity to be ‘work and take care of a man.’”
Outside, Wilson confirms to the producers that their relationship is over. “I feel like I might have failed,” he says.
Did Aneha Singh and Cam Halloran Get Married?
The first couple viewers see make it to their wedding day is Aneha Singh and Cam Halloran, who have had a rocky relationship since leaving the pods.

When she arrives at the venue, Aneha tells producers that Cam has the “pieces” to be the man she needs for the rest of her life. But, she is worried since her parents are not coming. Her sister Anekha arrives and seems to make Aneha more anxious.
Anekha says she is unsure Cam is the right person for her sister. She also tells Aneha she will not be happy if she says “yes” at the altar.

Cam appears calm while playing cards with his friends, although he shares he is nervous. He voices his concerns about Aneha’s family not meeting him, noting that he wants to have a relationship with his wife’s relatives.

When the ceremony begins, Aneha whispers to herself “What have you done?” She then canters down the aisle. She awkwardly says she doesn’t know what to do with her bouquet when she reaches Cam and the officiant, the first of many quips.

During his vows, Cam reflects on Aneha bringing him a sense of calm and comfort in the pods. In turn, she says during her vows that she hasn’t felt “enough” in past relationships and worried she would never find someone who loved all parts of her.

When asked to announce her decision, Aneha pauses and says she is feeling overwhelmed. “I need a second. I feel weird,” she repeats. After collecting herself, Aneha explains that while she feels like Cam is her “person,” she cannot marry him today.

Cam is understanding and says he wants both of them to be confident. They say they love each other and embrace while their guests applaud. As she departs, Aneha maintains that Cam is still her fiancé.

When she is alone, Aneha tells the cameras, “Cam at 28, just not husband material,” adding that he needs to be more communicative. “He needs more time. He’s not fully cooked yet,” she explains. However, she adds, “I’ve never loved someone like I love Cam.”
As for Cam, he says that it is “tough to be left at the altar” and reveals to his mom that he has always been bothered by Aneha’s family refusing to come to the wedding.
“She made the decision that was best for her and I don’t necessarily disagree with it. It feels like a failure which is sad,” he says.

When the two reunite, he seems unsure about continuing the relationship. He tells Aneha he needs to process what happened. In one of his final confessionals, he says it would be “somewhat of a fantasy world” to think he and Aneha could keep dating when they know it didn’t work out.
Did Sarah Williams and John Shannon Get Married?

Sarah Williams and John Shannon’s wedding day begins with the bride gushing about how happy she is as she arrives at the venue. While she gets her hair and makeup done, Sarah shares with friends and family some issues that have popped up in her relationship with John, like his opinions on the COVID-19 vaccine and how he “leads with distrust.”

She also reveals some of their off-camera conversations, mentioning John’s concern that she is a “consumer of politics” and would want to discuss the state of the world frequently. She then says John, 31, told her he believes single women over 30 are “problematic.”
John is shown chatting about his relationship with his family. He describes his fiancée as “a prize I’ll do anything for.”
“I feel the connection we made is enough to last the rest of our lives and I hope she feels the same way,” he tells the cameras.

At the altar, John says Sarah is beautiful, brilliant, thoughtful and kind in his vows. She reflects on their shaky beginning in the pods, recalling how they initially didn’t like each other. She says that unusual start has been the “catalyst” for their relationship. Sarah also praises John for being sensitive, funny, considerate and curious about the world.
Following their short vows, both say “I do,” making them the only Season 11 couple to tie the knot.
After the ceremony, John and Sarah tell producers how excited they are to be husband and wife. They are shown dancing and cutting their cake at the reception.
What Will Happen at the Reunion?
The teaser for the Season 11 reunion showed glimpses of explosive confrontations.
Michaella appears to argue with a fellow cast member, Jax and Stew confirm their relationship status and one person is questioned about being unfaithful.
“I’ll ask you point blank, did you cheat on your wife?” co-host Nick Lachey asks. He also says, “Whatever you’re trying to hide on this stage, it will come out.”
There could be a new couple that forms during the reunion. “Are you asking him out now?” co-host Vanessa Lachey says at one point.
Fans will be able to tune into all the drama when the reunion streams on Netflix Sunday, Nov. 8, at 6 p.m. PT/ 9 p.m. ET.

title: Barbara Walters Works a Shift at the Playboy Club in 1962
summary: Barbara Walters worked as a Playboy Bunny serving drinks at New York City’s Playboy Club in 1962.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Barbara Walters getting firsthand experience working at the famed Playboy Club in a segment that aired Dec. 31, 1962.

Barbara Walters was a pioneering journalist during her decades-long career. One of her most notable pieces aired on TODAY on Dec. 31, 1962, when she got dressed in the classic Playboy Bunny costume and worked a shift at the legendary New York City nightclub after learning what was involved and spoke with a few of the Bunnies.
She learned from chief of the Bunnies, Ms. Joan Howard, that anyone between the ages of 18 to 24, “young, pretty (and) funny” could become a Bunny.
They would then take a two-week course to learn their role at the club, which included not being able to date club members. Then it was Walters’ turn to learn the ropes.
“Off to Bunny school,” she said as her education started.

She put on the “too tight satin bathing suit and black leotard,” as she described it, along with shoes that were a size too big (“This job is hardest on the feet,” she said), a cotton tail, flashlight and pen hooked to her costume to take orders.
How Did Barbara Walters Feel in the Uniform?
As Walters, who died at the age of 93 in 2022, got into uniform and put on her ears, she asked if most of the girls are “embarrassed” when they first put on the costume.
“Not hardly,” replied the woman helping her. “I’d say one out of 143 might be embarrassed.”
“I think I’m two out of 143,” Walters said. “I feel ridiculous.”
Barbara Walters Learned the Bunny Rules

Walters explained how Bunnies have to learn the rules in the 35-page Bunny manual, including how to arrange a tray and what garnishes and glasses accompany each drink. Bunnies also had to take a test and follow the guidelines (no gum chewing, looking untidy or being late) outlined or risk getting fined. They had to refrain from dating customers or drinking before or on the job, which could result in termination.

After the test, the veteran servers worked with the trainees. In this instance, Walters struggled with a move called the Bunny Dip, which more experienced servers showed her was the proper way to hand drinks to customers. Walters then tried the move herself.
“It’s like a ballet movement,” she said.
How Did Barbara Walters Actually Do As a Bunny?
Walters then got her moment on the floor.
“I felt pretty awkward, but at least I didn’t spill anything on the customers,” she said.
Walters passed, but had no plans to stick with a career dishing out cocktails, even as TODAY anchor Hugh Downs praised her work when the segment ended.
“You make a very cute bunny,” he told her.

title: Elizabeth Holmes’ Partner, Billy Evans, Speaks Out Following the Release of ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, is sharing his thoughts on “You Can See Everything,” including what he believes is the biggest misconception about him and a slew of other topics.
story: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, is sharing his thoughts on “You Can See Everything,” including what he believes is the biggest misconception about him and a slew of other topics.
On Nov. 3, Evans invited people to participate in an AMA, ask me anything, on X, prefacing it needed “to be legally permisible (sic).”
Among the lightest questions include someone asking what the first thing he and Holmes will do after she is released from prison.
“Hold our kids tight and talk all night,” Evans, who shares two children with the Theranos founder replied.

Holmes was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what her company’s technology could do. She was sentenced to 11 years in prison in 2022 and is currently at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas.

“You Can See Everything,” the documentary by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, followed her and Evans weeks before she was incarcerated. The film has become a critical and commercial success, with many viewers and experts questioning her and Evans’ intentions.
Fielder had previously shared during a Los Angeles screening in October that Evans had yet to watch the film ahead of its Oct. 16 release.
When asked on X what he misses most about Holmes, Evans said “everything.”

“I miss her presence. Her touch. The way she runs her fingers through my hair. Her patience. She makes me a better person. And without her, I feel an emptiness that’s hard to describe,” he wrote. “People often say they need someone when what they really mean is that they want them. I’ve thought a lot about that distinction. I need Liz. She should qualify as a medically necessary prescription.”
When someone followed up by replying, “Her scrambled eggs,” Evans replied, “Def not this,” with a melting face emoji.

In the documentary, there’s a moment when Holmes is whisking eggs in a yellow bowl. As she’s speaking to Fielder, Evans grabs the bowl from her hands and starts to vigorously whip them. When the filmmaker questions his move, Evans implies it’s because his partner doesn’t do it right.

On X, Evans also shared he had seen “almost all of” Fielder’s work before filming “You Can See Everything.” He also wrote that they celebrated Fielder’s birthday “around the table in Del Mar with my family,” adding, “He also missed the Time 100 dinner, so we celebrated that too.”
TODAY.com did not immediately hear back from Evans, Fielder and Holmes when reached out for additional comment.
He also touched on more serious matters, including the “one misconception from the film” that he would like to dispel.

“That I somehow control Liz. Anyone who actually knows her would find that idea hilarious. She’s fiercely independent, strong-willed, and my best friend,” he tweeted. “We are partners in every sense. We challenge each other, disagree, and face the world together. Her closest friends are also some of my closest friends. If I ever mistreated her, they’d have my head.”
Someone also wondered why, in the documentary, he stopped Fielder from speaking to Holmes’ father.
“Both Nathan and the audience saw it as integral to the documentary to truly ‘see everything,’” the person wrote. “It felt like a missed opportunity that could have continued to give Liz more light.”

In his response, Evans noted that Holmes was going to prison and had three days together. “I wanted to spend that time together. He interviewed her parents after she went in. They chose not to include that in the film. I didn’t control the edit. If there was something the directors wanted from them they had multiple opportunities to get it.”

When questioned about using his power of attorney over Holmes and going directly to X instead of her for her profile password, he wrote that they “discussed this at length over several months. She knew exactly what we were doing.”

“We talk about everything, including X. Nothing happened behind her back,” he claimed. “The POA was simply the legal mechanism that allowed me to act on her behalf while she’s incarcerated. It was not a substitute for her consent.”
When pressed for more clarity, he replied that Holmes’ account was “tied to an old Theranos email. Password forgotten.”

“You Can See Everything” has continued to be a topic of conversation online. Whether the attention has been good or bad for Evans it’s unknown. However, when asked if he regretted agreeing to the documentary, he simply wrote, “Not at all.”

title: All Riley Green Wants for Christmas Is...
summary: Riley Green chats with TODAY.com about what’s on his holiday wishlist, favorite holiday memories and tradition he’d like to continue when he has a family.
story: Life is keeping Riley Green busy.

The 38-year-old country crooner has been spending his time on the road following the release of his “That’s Just Me” album, as well as in Los Angeles after becoming the latest addition to “The Voice.”
He jokes that the lyric from his latest album that best describes his life right now is “think as you drunk.”
“It’s how I feel most of the time,” he tells TODAY.com with a laugh. “Not from drinking, just from being exhausted”

“It’s been a wild ride the last few years. I’ve grown so much and I’m super blessed to be able to do what I’m doing,” he continues. “But a lot of things have popped up that I didn’t think I was going to be doing on top of touring, like ‘The Voice’ and flying to LA every week filming. That’s a really new gig and a new experience for me, but something that’s been really fun to do.”
Green still has a busy schedule for the rest of the year. But as the days get darker and the festive season kicks off, there’s definitely one thing that is on the country superstar’s wish list.

“Some time off,” he quips, sharing what he wants for Christmas. “If I get to go home and spend some time with the family and have some nice, cool weather days to get out in the woods, I think I’ll be really happy.”
Having a booked schedule, he says, has reminded him of how important it is to have “a little bit of time at the farm” and disconnect from the outside world.

“I think the busier you are, the more you need that, and the more successful you are, the more you need that,” Green says. “I think everybody needs to be reminded that you’re still a regular dude. And going back to Alabama, I’m certainly reminded of that. My buddies don’t let me forget.”

That’s why any chance he gets to unwind and get comfortable is a win in Green’s book.  The “My Way” singer gets to do just that as the new face of Hey Dude’s “It’s a Comfort Miracle” campaign, where he gets to kick off his boots and relax.

“I grew up in Alabama. My granddaddy was a really laid back guy, loved to go fishing and golfing. And when I’m home, that’s kind of my break from boots,” Green says, sharing some of his favorite ways to unwind after a hard day’s work.

“Nap usually,” he says. “When I get to my farm in Alabama, I love to get on a tractor and clear some land or till up and plant a green field. I like being able to see what you get done at the end of the day.”

Green fans, meanwhile, can do a bit of unwinding themselves. As part of the collab, people can watch him in a festive sweater and comfy shoes, strumming his guitar next to a Christmas tree in his own version of a fireplace yule log.
Reflecting on the holidays, the “Worst Way” singer calls getting a drum set as a kid his “favorite Christmas gift.” But his most cherished memory was being surrounded by family.

“Both sets of grandparents would come over Christmas morning, and we’d kind of stretch it out for a week going to visit everybody,” he says. “Family being around everybody is something that I’ve always really enjoyed, and now I probably appreciate it more than ever.”
He says a tradition he would love to continue when he starts his own family would be, “Going to grandmother’s house and opening presents.”
“And the cooking,” he adds, noting his love for his mom’s breakfast casserole and sweet potato casserole.

“We would do breakfast at my grandmother’s house. She made really good biscuits and gravy,” Green says. “I think that I would love for my family to be able to experience some of the home-cooked meals that I got growing up and going to those family gatherings.”

title: ‘DWTS’ Dancer Falls Mid-Routine, But You Can’t Even Tell: ‘Most Iconic Recovery In History’
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” troupe member Diego Pasillas reacts to his fall during the “Disney Night” episode.
story: The opening number of the latest “Dancing With the Stars” episode had a slight mistake that some viewers barely noticed thanks to one dancer’s impressive recovery.

The Nov. 2 episode of the dancing competition series, Disney Night, opened with Broadway-inspired routines celebrating productions like “The Lion King,” “Beauty and the Beast,” “Newsies,” “The Greatest Showman” and “Aladdin.” Each musical was highlighted with performances featuring the “DWTS” troupe and pros. But one member of the troupe had an unexpected moment in the spotlight when he briefly slipped.
After the “Newsies” section began, dancer Diego Pasillas glided onto the stage and stumbled before popping up and hitting his next move, without missing a beat.
Pasillas reacted to his fall in a video shared on Instagram following the performance. “Guys, I just ate it on national television,” he said as he laughed.

He then included a slow-motion TikTok clip of the mishap before nailing the correct move. “But instead I did,” he added and re-created the slip. He showed how he turned the fall into a half split and bounced back onto his feet.
“The show must go on,” Pasillas cheekily said.
Fans in the comments applauded Pasillas’ positive attitude, pointing out how he wasn’t fazed by the error.
“This was the most iconic recovery in HISTORY,” one praised.
Another joked, “That was NOT a mistake. It was an ‘unexpected solo.’”

A third commented, “Every dance teacher is going to play this clip from here on out to teach their dancers what owning their mistakes and good recovery techniques can do for a performer. truly a masterclass.”
Even a few pros chimed in to show support for a member of their “DWTS” family.
Val Chmerkovskiy quipped, “Bro you shablammed it and then shamblammed it in the air.”
New pro Hailey Bills wrote, “BUT THE WAY YOU GOT UP” and “PROFESSIONAL BADDIE” in another comment.
On his Instagram story, Pasillas shared more sweet messages from viewers who complimented his professionalism.

Pasillas’ and the rest of the dancers’ lively opening number set the tone for the night. Stars like Amber Glenn, Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr. performed routines to classic Disney songs throughout the evening. All the stars were then divided into two teams of four for group dances set to songs from “Zootopia 2” and “High School Musical.”
At the end of the night, it was announced that Julia Stiles and her partner Ezra Sosa were eliminated from the competition.
“It’s been an incredible experience,” Stiles said before expressing her gratitude for her partner.

title: Stevie Van Zandt Reveals His Role In James Gandolfini’s Casting as Tony Soprano: ‘I’m Not Sure He Ever Knew’
summary: Stevie Van Zandt famously played Tony Soprano’s right hand man, but the E Street Band musician says he almost landed the lead.
story: Stevie Van Zandt famously played Tony Soprano’s right hand man, but the E Street Band musician says he almost landed the lead.
Van Zandt talked all things Springsteen and “The Sopranos” in an interview with TODAY’s Craig Melvin for the Nov. 3 episode of his podcast, “Glass Half Full.”

Van Zandt told Craig he originally had “no interest” in acting, not even when he first got a call from television writer and producer David Chase. Chase, the creator of “The Sopranos,” saw Van Zandt’s “comical introduction” of The Rascals during their Rock & Roll Hall of Fall induction in 1997, the first time the ceremony had ever been televised.
As Van Zandt tells it, Chase tracked the musician down through his foundation and called him with an offer: “Hey, man, I’m doing a new TV show, you want to be in it?”
“I’m like, ‘No, not really,’” Van Zandt recalled.
Van Zandt had no acting experience at the time.
“He says, ‘Don’t worry. You are an actor. You just don’t know it yet,’” Van Zandt said. “... I had nothing else to do, right?”
Van Zandt, who went on to play Silvio Dante across all six seasons of the mob show, still had to formally audition for the show for Chase.
“I went down there, and he liked what I did so much, believe it or not, he cast me as Tony Soprano,” Van Zandt said.
As a “little formality,” Van Zandt said Chase had him audition again for HBO on the West Coast. When the musician arrived for his audition, he saw James Gandolfini waiting.
Van Zandt had just seen the actor in 1993’s “True Romance.” He said he told a casting director, “That’s the cat that should be playing Tony Soprano.”

“I put it in her head because I said, ‘You know who that is?’ She said, no. I said, ‘I just saw him in a movie. Believe me, he’s the one who should be playing Tony Soprano.’ And she looked at me like I had two heads,” Van Zandt said.

After Van Zandt auditioned again, his casting was vetoed due to the musician’s lack of experience. Chase then told Van Zandt he could “have any other part” he wanted, but he said he started to feel guilty “taking an actor’s job.” Van Zandt’s wife, Maureen, is an actor, and he had witnessed all the work she put into her career.
“He says, ‘OK, I’m gonna write you in a part that doesn’t exist. You ain’t taking nobody’s job,’” Van Zandt said.
Craig asked if Gandolfini, who died in June 2013, ever thanked Van Zandt for his part in his casting.
“I’m not sure he ever knew,” Van Zandt said.
“I don’t know, and I don’t know if I was the only factor there,” he continued. “But once they saw him, I mean, he was just so great. I mean, what a loss.
“Loss, personally, but also, he’s just one of the great actors of all time,” he added. “And he would have been legendary. He is anyway.”

title: Carson Daly Joins TODAY in 2013 With the Debut of the Orange Room
summary: Look back on Carson Daly’s first day at TODAY in September 2013, when he introduced viewers to the show’s digital home, the Orange Room. He also shows off the updated space.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Carson Daly joining the program on Sept. 12, 2013.
Carson Daly couldn’t wait to get to work when he became part of the TODAY family. And all these years later, he is still part of the show’s major moments.

When Carson officially joined TODAY on Sept. 12, 2013, he had already made a name for himself as host of MTV’s “Total Request Live” and NBC’s “The Voice.” At the time, he was tapped as the host of the Orange Room, serving as a digital liaison that connected TODAY and its audience.
Thirteen years later, Carson, along with Savannah Guthrie, Craig Melvin, Al Roker and Jenna Bush Hager, looked back at Carson’s first day, when he formally introduced viewers to the Orange Room.
“I had to create my own little world here just to be a part of this historic show. We were the nexus point between the broadcast and the audience at home,” Carson said Nov. 3 on TODAY.
He then debuted what the Orange Room looks like now, as well as its new name: the TODAY Lounge.
“It’s called the TODAY Lounge now. That’s where our digital producers capture content and post on social media throughout the morning,” Craig added.
Carson’s role has certainly changed over the years, but he’s remained a staple of the show — and the voice of a generation. Below, revisit Carson’s TODAY debut, which can also be seen here.
Joining TODAY Was a Natural Fit for Carson
When Carson first joined TODAY, he was more than ready to give morning television a try.
“I think a lot of people associate me more with nighttime. Truth be told, I’m really a morning person. And now the TODAY show comes along,” he said at the time.

“Over 60 years of incredible morning television, and now what feels like the beginning of a new era of today,” he added. “Just recently, when I was asked to be a part of this new exciting room within Studio 1A called the Orange Room, I was blown away. The TODAY show viewer feels like they have a home. They can contact me, whether it’s tweeting and social media.”
Carson Has Always Been a TODAY Fan
Carson also shared his longtime affinity for TODAY.

“When I’m there, I feel like a kid in the candy store. I think the first time I was on TODAY, I was having so much fun, and I tweeted, ‘TODAY show is “TRL” for grown-ups,’” he added. “Look, I mean, it’s the TODAY show. I feel like I’ve been adopted by the first family.”
What Carson Envisioned About Being on TODAY
In 2013, Carson was eager to connect with fans and share his own life with viewers. He jokingly called himself a “welcome mat for TODAY show audience.”
“I’ll be your digital doormat,” he said about his role. It was an assignment he couldn’t wait to tackle.
“It really is the most fun you can possibly imagine,” he added.

title: Amor Towles Told Jenna Bush Hager About Having Tea with Her Parents — and the Moment He Still ‘Can’t Believe’ Happened
summary: Amor Towles and Jenna Bush Hager had a bonding moment when he stopped by her podcast, “Open Book with Jenna.”
story: Amor Towles and Jenna Bush Hager had a bonding moment when he stopped by her podcast, “Open Book with Jenna.”
It turns out Towles once spent a conversation-filled afternoon with Jenna’s parents, former President George W. Bush and Laura Bush.

The Bushes are both fans of Towles’ second book, “A Gentleman in Moscow,” published in 2016, and invited him for tea when he was visiting Dallas in 2022. (Jenna is also a fan of Towles — she picked his third book, “The Lincoln Highway,” for her book club in 2021).
“We had a wonderful hour talking about the book,” he told Jenna Bush Hager on the Oct. 29 episode of Open Book with Jenna.

“We had tea. They wanted to talk about the book and my process. Why did I do this and how did I do that. Just like they were any other readers in the country,” Towles said. “All the presidency stuff falls away. You’re just talking to enthusiastic readers.”

Towles said they finished their tea and shook hands to say goodbye. On the way out, Towles decided to mention headlines that were relevant to the Moscow-set book. Russia had just invaded Ukraine the day before their chat.
“It was really quite something that this just happened,” Towles said. “I just said to your dad, ‘This news is really troubling. I can imagine it must be something for your perspective.
“He paused and said, ‘Have a seat.’ Then we spent an hour talking about Russia, and his life in the White House,” he said.
Towles said his reaction to the conversation’s turn was one of shock and delight.

“I can’t believe what was happening. This is crazy. I was just a kid from Dedham, Massachusetts who wanted to write stories. Here I am, talking to a president about the head of Russia the day after the invasion about what was happening behind-the-scenes. It’s just mind-blowing.”
He feels gratitude for the way his work affects people and opens up his world.
“From the person you’ve never met, where it’s touched them in a private, personal way, to the book opening to the door to a conversation you can’t believe you’re having,” he said.
